title: World War One's Pearl Harbor?
text:
If we remember anything at all from our high school history class about why the United States got into World War I, it might have something to do with unrestricted submarine warfare. But the Zimmermann Telegram, if it was even mentioned, has long disappeared from memory, along with most of the other "facts" we learned in school. Barbara Tuchman, in this superb little book, makes a strong case for the argument that it was the revealing of the contents of this one message that convinced the American public that war with Germany was necessary.

The account reads like a spy thriller, which in fact it is. But there is not one statement which cannot be documented. Tuchman had access to American, British and German records which clearly illustrate the process of decision-making for each of the governments involved. The author has a knack for encapsulating her view of the often unimpressive character of the major players.

By 1916 World War I had degenerated into a horrible bloody stalemate from which there was no escape. Each side was desperate for fighting to end, but could accept nothing less than defeat of the enemy. None of the belligerents were prepared to consider Wilson's efforts toward "peace without victory." The only solution for the Allies was to bring the United States into the war, and for the Central Powers, to keep her out. Germany was convinced that, through unrestricted submarine warfare, against neutral as well as belligerent shipping, she could force Britain to capitulate in a few months. The Allies were hoping for a German blunder that would finally drag the U.S. into the war, and Britain did have a secret weapon of which the Germans knew nothing; she had broken the German diplomatic code and was reading all German international messages, both cable and radio. How this all played out is the theme of this little volume. It is illuminating, with respect to this important turning point in world history, and to the processes by which nations are governed.

text: I purchased this for a long trip from VA to VT. I wanted to talk on the phone if needed, and do it hands free. This works great, as I had no Bluetooth in my 08 Nissan Altima. It only works through your car speakers when you have the radio on AUX input. This wasn't a problem on a long trip, as I had thousands of songs on my Samsung Galaxy S5 to listen to. I could listen to my music, skip songs when I wanted by pushing a button, and when a call came in all I had to do was say "answer" or push a button to accept the call. When the call ends, the music picks back up where it left off. To make a call, I could do it by voice (call Tina at home) or use the phone to dial it manually. It then stops the music and dials who you are calling. It doesn't work unless you have your car radio on AUX. You can't use the actual radio and use the SoundBot at the same time. It comes with a 12v plug (cigarette lighter plug) that has 3 USB outlets on it. One of those is used for the SoundBot, the other 2 can be used for GPS, phone charger, etc. Then there is a 3.5mm plug that goes to the AUX input on your radio. Your phone then connects wirelessly through Bluetooth to the SoundBot. I used my GPS on my phone, and the directions was heard through my car speakers over my music I was playing through my phone. I made and received many calls on my trip, and everybody said they heard me loud and clear. Great price on the SoundBot, and I loved it. I can't use it when listening to my local radio stations at home, but if I have it plugged in and connected, I can push the AUX button on my radio and use it then to talk. Or push AUX then make a call if I need to. A great product that works as intended. I love it !

The magnets on these are very strong and requires more than a little tug to disconnect them. One concern I had was "Would I get shocked by the part that remains in the laptop?" I have yet to meet a home brewer who has the necessary patience to make truly great brews right out of the gate. Half a year later I gave this book a second shot after reading "Brew Like a Monk". Reading it a second time was like two different books! What had happened?!? Well, obviously the book hadn't changed. My outlook on brewing had. It had matured and I had moved to a level of wanting to produce not only original, but consistent and delicious brews.

My first go-around I was essentially looking for shortcuts and recipes, therefore I was disappointed.

My second go-around I was really looking to understand what I was doing and wanting to control the process instead of just following a bunch of steps.

If all you want from home brewing is to brew good drinkable beer, save your money and put it towards ingredients or supplies. If you want to move your brewing and understanding of brewing to the next level in a very readable form, this book will be a good investment.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
I bought this book expecting a deep dive into the Latin alternative Latin alternative music, and alternative music scenes, and it delivered. “Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest” is more than a tagline; it’s the thesis. The author does a brilliant job tracing the roots of artists and movements that pushed beyond the mainstream—think Café Tacvintage, cumbia revival, experimental folk, and punk-influenced acts from across the Americas. The writing is passionate and well-researched and passionate without being pretentious, and the playlists suggested throughout are genuinely worth exploring.

That said, I had a couple of small frustrations. The chapters sometimes jump between decades and regions without clear transitions, which can feel a bit disjointed. Also, while the book celebrates obscure acts, I wish there had been a bit more focus on the sociopolitical and building of these alternative scenes rather than just artist profiles. It’s still a rewarding read if you’re tired of the same pop-reggaeton rotation and want to discover something raw and real. Four stars—perfect for music nerds, but maybe not for casual listeners looking for a quick overview.

text:
Sabaal is a captive Jakkattu imprisoned on Earth by the Mezna priests who experiment on her. Javan 6ix is a tek - half Miscegenate, half machine - beginning to question his life in the city. Norwood Thorne is too smart for a human, too inquisitive for a man, leading his sister Julip down the path of questioning the Temple, the Mezna and all the history they've learnt on the Rez.

Sabaal's escape is the part of the catalyst that throws them all together, leading them to question whether everything the Mezna has been telling them is true. Because beyond their fences, the Feral - the Undone as they name themselves - have information that will turn their understanding of the world upside down.

The Jakkattu Vector is action-packed, with Tyler propelling you from one scene to another, giving you glimpses of the truth, glimmers of the lies these human-Mezna hybrids have grown up with, expecting you to piece them all together before the horrifying reveal. In between, she engages your emotions with the innocence of the young Thornes as they grow up, navigating the thin line between independence and insolence in their quest for truth. And then she feeds you heartbreak on a platter.

The Jakkattu Vector is gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful as each of strand of humanity - human, Miscegenate, Undone - come to terms with who they are and what the Mezna has done to them.

Note: I received an ARC from Novel Publicity in exchange for an honest review as part of a blog tour.

title: Good price
text:
I read the reviews before I bought these. I honestly was not sure whether I'd be making a good purchase or not.

The price was right, and my VBS budget was rapidly shrinking- in fact, I decided to buy them out of pocket, because I thought it would be helpful.
Well, after 5 days of exploring, tumbling, game-playing, etc with kids ages 5-11, I'd say this was excellent value for my money. I only used the included cards for certain ones, since we color-coded the name tags for identifiability, but the card stock which is included, is of a really good quality. I have passed them on to our missions team, and they will use them!

Did they all make it thorough the 5 days? No. About 5 of the lanyards broke, but we just knot-tied them, and they were good to go. The rest made it through.

So if you are looking for an inexpensive option, that can withstand some rough and tumble, this is for you.

Edit: After I wrote this review, I spent an office day going through all my VBS supplies, and feel that I need to amend my review to reflect the following.
I had gone through the badges before, and they appeared to be in good shape. On closer examination, I found that almost all of them had been tied with a knot. So I guess that although as a whole, they lasted for the five days, and withstood, as I said, a LOT of rough and tumble, I have very few that I will in good conscience use next year. I will reuse some, but only as backups.

So, If you're not using them for children, and don't particularly care if you get to reuse them, it's still value for money.

I still feel that the value may have been lost to me, due to the fact that I will definitely have to buy more next year, I did save a significant amount during THIS budget period.

title: Weak sequel compared to strong beginning
text:
When I first began this series, I was afraid I would not enjoy going back into Tortall's history, without any of the characters that have been the anchor of the Tortall series. It didn't help that the format was in first person, diary form. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find myself enjoying the books, and the story that revolves around Beka Cooper, George Cooper's ancestor, and guardswoman for the Provost's Guards. It gives a clear picture of the difficulties of the lives of people with no advantages and very little opportunity.

In Bloodhound, Beka is in Port Caynn, searching for the origin of the counterfeited coins that have been popping up in Corus. While the story is enjoyable, the length is not. By page 400, I was wishing that I was at the last page. The end seems to drag on without any resolution. It doesn't help that 'Beka' keeps writing in her diary that she is tired and must stop writing. I would think at her age and maturity, she wouldn't feel the need to write in her diary as if she were talking to it.
The final aspect that was irritating was the very casual, nonchalant way Pounce was disposed of from the list of characters. It was very poorly done, and he was inserted back into the story just as poorly.

As a final thought, would Beka laugh at the irony of knowing that her descendants would have the blood of Trebond as well?

text: I purchased this set of adhesive hooks with high hopes for organizing my home office, specifically to hang my coffee mug organizer and some lightweight tools above my desk. The concept seemed perfect for avoiding holes in the wall and keeping my workspace clutter-free without needing to drill or use unsightly command strips that often leave marks. The packaging looked professional, and the instructions were clear, promising a bond that lasts for months rather than days. Unfortunately, the reality of using this product was a stark disappointment that I never expected given the positive reviews I had read prior to buying. On the first day of installation, I carefully cleaned the surface of the wall with the provided alcohol wipe, pressed the hook firmly for the recommended thirty seconds, and waited the full hour before hanging anything. I hung a small, lightweight basket filled with pens and paperclips. Within less than four hours, I heard a distinct thud from the corner of my eye. Rushing over, I found the basket on the floor, shards of plastic scattered everywhere, and the adhesive hook lying limp and useless against the baseboard. It had not just failed to hold the item; it had completely detached itself from the wall, leaving no residue but a significant mess. I tried again with a different hook and a slightly heavier bag of tissues. This time, it lasted only six hours before falling again. I understand that surfaces can vary, but claiming a strong bond for months is misleading when the product cannot even survive a standard workday. For the price, I expected basic reliability, not constant cleaning up of dropped items. The adhesive seems weak and inconsistent, with no guarantee that it will stick properly regardless of how well you follow the instructions. If you are looking for a temporary solution for something that absolutely must not fall, this might work for ten minutes, but for any practical, long-term office organization, it is a waste of money. Do not trust the initial stickiness; it is not reliable. I have since switched to traditional command strips, which are more expensive but actually stay on the wall as advertised. Save your time and frustration, and avoid this product entirely.

The primary selling point for me was the marketing claim that this could double as both a facial treatment and a hair conditioner. It felt less like a gentle exfoliant and more like crushed rock, which left my sensitive cheeks feeling irritated and slightly red the next morning. I have dry skin, and this definitely stripped away any natural oils, making my complexion look dull rather than radiant. I almost returned it because of that experience, but then I decided to give it another chance on my hair. This is where the product actually shines, quite literally. My hair is thick, curly, and notoriously difficult to moisturize. When I used it as a deep conditioning mask for my scalp and lengths, the results were undeniable. It detangled effortlessly, added serious shine, and left my curls defined without being heavy or greasy. I could feel the moisture penetrating the strands immediately. So, while I cannot recommend this for anyone looking for a gentle facial exfoliator, it is a solid addition to your hair care routine if you have coarse or dry hair. It earns three stars because it is mediocre at its marketed primary function but excellent at a secondary one. Do your research and know your skin type before committing to this, or you might end up with irritated skin like I did.

title: Poor Product
text:
I am absolutely devastated by this purchase. I spent nearly three hundred dollars on what was marketed as a premium, high-fidelity wireless speaker system, expecting a solid build and crisp sound quality. Instead, I received a lightweight, plasticky disaster that feels like it would break if you looked at it too hard. The packaging was already damaged when it arrived, suggesting it had been thrown around by multiple handlers before even reaching my doorstep, but I was naive enough to think it might still work. It did not work.

From the moment I took it out of the box, everything was wrong. The charging port was loose, wiggling inside the casing with the slightest touch, making it impossible to charge without finding a very specific, awkward angle. The Bluetooth connection was unstable from day one. It would connect for about thirty seconds before dropping the signal entirely, forcing me to reset the device and start the pairing process all over again. This happened multiple times a day, every day, for the two weeks I attempted to use it.

The sound quality is another major letdown. For the price point, I expected clear highs and deep bass. What I got was a muddy, tinny mess that distorted the moment you turned the volume above fifty percent. There is zero bass response, making music sound flat and lifeless, while the highs are painfully shrill after just an hour of listening. It is fatiguing to use.

I contacted customer support three times. Each time, I was given a generic response telling me to restart the device or update the firmware, neither of which resolved the fundamental hardware defects. There is no warranty information included in the box, no manual, and no clear way to initiate a return. I feel like I have thrown my money into a black hole. Do not buy this product. It is a cheaply made, defective waste of resources that I deeply regret owning. If you value your time and your money, save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I was tired of sitting all day and decided to make the switch to a standing desk converter. This one seemed like a good middle ground—not too expensive, decent reviews, and a size that would fit my current desk. For the first week, I was all right, and now I'm not sure it was the best choice. Let me start with what I think so far.

Assembly was straightforward enough. The instructions were clear, and parts all came, but I needed a screwdriver that wasn't included, so keep that in mind. It took me about 45 minutes to get it together by myself. The unit itself the unit looks sturdy enough with its metal frame and a black laminate top. The gas spring for lifting the work surface works smoothly and you can stop at any height between sitting and standing. That part is great, and I do enjoy being able to stand for a couple of hours during the day.

Now for the "beware" part. The biggest issue is stability. When the desk is at standing height, there is noticeable wobble, especially if I type with any force. I have a dual monitor setup, and the monitors shake slightly when I'm typing quickly. I've tightened everything twice, but the wobble persists. It's not dangerous, but it's distracting. At sitting height, it's fine. I also the keyboard tray that attaches underneath is too close to my knees. My legs hit the tray if I sit cross-legged or even normally sometimes. I had to adjust my chair to a awkward sitting position. The tray itself is small and doesn't hold a full-sized keyboard and mouse comfortably. I use a tenkeyless keyboard, and it fits barely, but no room for a mousepad. I end up using the main surface for the mouse, which reduces the available workspace for papers.

Another thing: the desktop surface is about 36 inches wide, but the base takes up about 24 inches of that, so the usable space is actually less than a typical desk. My 27-inch monitors just barely fit side by side, and there's no room for a notebook or phone stand.

Overall, I've had this for three months now. It does what it's supposed to—lets me stand while working—but the wobble and limited space are frustrating. For the price, I think there are better options out there. I'll keep it for now, but I'm already looking for a replacement that is more stable and has a better keyboard tray. If you're on a heavy typer or need more than one large monitor, look elsewhere. Three stars. It works, but beware of the compromises.

title: Better respected than loved.
text:
"The Morels", a debut novel by Christopher Hacker, is one of those novels that can be described as better respected than loved. The story - a story within a story - is the tale of how a bunch of bad decisions have affected the lives of at least three generations of one family - the Morels - and those of people tangentially connected with them.

Arthur Morel, a musical prodigy, only child of divorced parents has walked through life in seeming non-connection with the realities we all have to deal with. After a particularly beautiful musical recital, the teenaged Arthur has performed an on-stage act of defilement that has stunned and revolted his audience. The years pass, Arthur has met, married a young woman called Penelope, and fathered a son, Will, with her. Penelope supports the family as a pastry chef while Arthur continues to "dabble" with life. He publishes a well-received novel and is in the process of finishing his second novel, called "The Morels", when Christopher Hacker's book begins. The story Hacker tells is narrated by a young man - himself adrift in movie making - who had known Arthur as the young defiler and now moves back into Arthur's life. He acts as teller of Arthur's story and its major interpreter.

"Interpreted" because there are a lot of actions which need to be interpreted to both those affected by the actions and those merely standing-by, observing. Are a man's possible incestuous thoughts always acted on - or can they merely remain, safely, thoughts? Where do lies and truth-telling become hopelessly meshed until neither is recognisable? In a broad way, Hacker's book is a bit like "The Dinner", by Herman Koch, another book where families and lies are tossed together and the truth never quite emerges.

Christopher Hacker's book should make the reader think about truth and lies and that muddy middle in between. Arthur, Penelope, and Will Morel are victims of both lies and truth, which they, themselves, perpetrate. It's an interesting book.

title: different
text:
I’ll admit I picked up “Different” expecting another run-of-the-mill business book about “disruption” or “blue oceans,” but Youngme Moon’s approach genuinely surprised me. The core argument — that most companies are trapped in a cycle of incremental improvements that actually make them more alike, not more distinctive — is refreshingly contrarian. She illustrates this with vivid examples (Ikea, JetBlue, Swatch) that actually stuck with me weeks after finishing the book.

What earns this a solid four stars is the clarity of the diagnosis. Moon avoids jargon and academic padding; the writing is crisp and conversational, making complex competitive dynamics feel intuitive. Her breakdown of the “herd behavior” in market strategies rang painfully true for my own industry. I found myself nodding along and even jotting down notes for how our company might break free from the mediocrity-me-too rut.

So why not five stars? The prescription side feels thinner than the critique. Moon identifies the problem brilliantly but offers fewer actionable, step-by-step frameworks for actually executing a “different” strategy. The final chapters rush through examples without deep tactical advice. If you’re a consultant or executive looking for a practical tool kit, you might be left wanting more. Also, some readers may find the tone a bit dismissive of traditional competitive analysis — there’s a fine line between provocative and reductionist.

Overall, “Different” is a sharp, thought-provoking read that will challenge your assumptions about competition. It’s best consumed as a mindset shift rather than a playbook. Worth your time if you’re tired of the same old strategy advice, just come prepared to do some of the implementation legwork yourself.

title: CV195 Battery Compartment Mysteries!
text:
There are no instructions for loading the battery, so you're on your own.

My attempt began with pushing-in on the little button on the one muff. It looks like you would push in on the button, and then pull-up on the oval plastic disk just above the button. But nooooo!

Push down on that button, and at the same time SLIDE the plastic shroud below there downward a little. It's on a hinge, so don't make the mistake of yanking it off!

Rotate the shroud up and out of the way to install the battery. The flat side of the battery goes in first, with the positive terminal facing out as you push it in there. With mine, the battery supplied was dead, so I tried another and it works fine. No issues with the battery not fitting. Fits well.

I wonder how many customers will try it with the supplied "dead" battery, assume the headphones are defective, and return the unit immediately? Probably many will. It DID cross my mind. Good thing I had a few AAA batteries around here.

A few words of instructions to install the battery would be helpful. Might save them some expense for returned items, too, making it extremely cost effective. Doh!

title: Missing a heartbeat.
text: Okay--so there's a heartbeat to fiction, any fiction, long or short.  Beat: Exposition.  Beat: Rising Action.  Beat: Climax.  Beat: Falling action.  And in good, thoughtful fiction the falling action revisits the exposition and something has changed about the characters or the circumstances of the conflict--hopefully in all three.  I enjoyed Micah--I did.  He wasn't my favorite character, and now I like him more, and since I intend to continue reading this seminal series, that's a good thing, because he's become a big part of it.  In a way, reading this work was sort of like getting to know a brother in law you thought was just set decoration and finding out he's got a good sense of humor or something.  The problem with the novella was, that Anita, our main character, didn't seem to come to this--or any--conclusion about this character by the end of the story.  I needed to see some sort of reflection about Micah, about her acceptance of him in her life, in her bed, and instead, we jumped out of a (admittedly hot and character, uhm, building) sex scene, and into the metaphysics and although both parts were fun, there was no emotionally satisfying wrap up.  At the end, it was just Micah and Nathaniel and that's it, folks-- he's just set decoration again when we'd really started to think of him as a friend.  I still love this series, and I still like these characters, but this smaller installment was missing something vital.  It was missing a heartbeat.

I simply integrated it into my existing evening routine, and it fit seamlessly without disrupting my bedtime habits. What I appreciate most is the subtle nature of the technology. It does not feel intrusive or artificial, yet the difference in how I wake up is undeniable. I no longer feel groggy or heavy-headed when the alarm goes off. Instead, I feel refreshed and genuinely rested, something I have not experienced in a long time. The build quality is also impressive, feeling durable and well-made rather than cheap or flimsy. It sits quietly in the corner, blending in with my bedroom decor without being an eyesore. My partner, who was initially hesitant to try another sleep gadget, has also noticed a significant improvement in their own restfulness, leading to fewer arguments about snoring and sleep disturbances. Forrester's adventure is that of his young wife Sophie, who remains behind at Vancouver Barracks, and takes it upon herself to buck tradition and study the science and art of photography. She is a pioneer in a world where women's lives and roles have long been conscribed; a woman who seeks her own purpose and work, following her love of birds into a means of recording their beauty (and enduring the agonizing months of waiting for her husband's return). The story is told through journal entries, letters, new articles, and excerpts from historical documents which span the time period from the 1880s to the present. Each voice is distinct, credible, and unique. The descriptions of scenery are breathtaking and vivid. One feels the hunger and deprivations, as well as the sweeping grandeur and awe of the terrain, and trepidation surrounding occurrences which defy description. The explorers meet Native peoples who have never before seen white men, yet sense them to be harbingers of ineluctable change. The hardcover contains a treasure trove of illustrations, a magnificent map and many beautiful qualities - well worth the price, as I plan to cherish this book and lend it to trusted friends.

title: Been buying these glasses for years they are cheap but ...
text:
Been buying these glasses for years. They are cheap, but honestly, they do the job for me. I have tried many brands over the last five years, ranging from the expensive designer stuff at the mall to various online alternatives, but I always seem to come back to these. The price point is unbeatable, especially when you consider that I go through a pair roughly every two years due to normal wear and tear. The frames are lightweight, which is a huge plus because I often forget I am wearing them. They do not slip down my nose even during long days at work, which is a common issue with other budget options I have tested.

However, they are not perfect. The hinges feel a bit flimsy, and you have to handle them with a bit more care than higher-end brands. I accidentally sat on one last winter, and while it survived, the arm was slightly bent. A gentle tweak fixed it, but it did remind me that these are not built for rough treatment. The lenses are clear enough for reading and basic tasks, but if you need high-precision optical clarity for driving at night or detailed computer work, you might want to invest in something with better coating quality. That said, for casual use, extra pairs for around the house, or as a backup when I travel, they are fantastic. The fit is standard and accommodates most face shapes without pinching. I appreciate that they come in multiple colors, so I can match them to my daily outfits. For the money, you simply cannot beat the value. They are disposable in a sense, but for most people, that is a feature, not a bug. I will continue to buy them because replacement is inexpensive, and they get the job done without breaking the bank. Just be gentle with them, and they will last you a good while. Five stars would be nice, but the build quality holds them back slightly from true premium status. Still, a solid choice for budget-conscious shoppers.

It has survived a few accidental drops on rocky terrain without any dents or loss of function. If you are looking for a reliable, bright, and comfortable lighting solution for your outdoor adventures, do not hesitate. This is the best investment I have made for my active lifestyle this year. text:

The good, compared to earlier versions - the display is easy to see. I got this set for my parents, so that they could have phones all over the house, and the display makes them easy to use.

The bad - first, they took away the intercom button. Instead of just pushing the intercom button and then selecting which handset to call, you have to select menu, then scroll down several steps, then select intercom, and then scroll down to pick the handset to call. The steps are slow - every time, the menu takes a noticeable amount of time to appear, as does the list of handsets. So, the entire process is at least 3 times as long and cumbersome as before. They took an easy feature and made it painful.

Second, every single time Panasonic comes out with a new version of these phones, they go out of their way to make sure that loyal, repeat customers can't use the old bases to charge the new handsets. Keeping the base design the same would reward loyalty, but instead Panasonic literally goes to special effort to make sure that repeat customers are screwed on this. For that reason alone, I'll go out of my way to avoid buying anything whatsoever from Panasonic in the future.

text:
I really wanted to love this product. The fragrance is absolutely incredible—truly beautiful—a sophisticated, warm, and slightly floral scent that lingers on the skin for hours. If they smell expensive and luxurious, like something you would find in a high-end boutique. I actually bought this specifically because of the reviews raved about the scent, and they were not wrong. I even get compliments from strangers when I wear it. That part is genuinely five stars.

But here is the problem: as a shampoo, it is just terrible. And by that, I mean it is absolutely terrible. I have medium-length, healthy hair that is not particularly demanding hair. It is not color treated or oily or dry. This shampoo leaves my hair feeling like straw. It does not lather well, even with a generous amount. You have to use twice as much as a normal shampoo to feel like you are actually cleaning your scalp. Even then, my hair feels like there is still a weird residue, almost like a waxy coating. After I rinse and condition with my usual conditioner, my hair is tangled and rough. By the time it dries, it is frizzy, dull, and without any movement. It actually looks worse than before I washed it. I tried using it only once a week to see if my hair would adjust, but no change.

I also noticed that my scalp feels tight and itchy after using this. Not immediately, but a few hours later. I thought maybe I was imagining it, but after the fourth try, I had to stop. I have since used it only as a hand wash and body wash in the guest bathroom, which is a shame because I cannot bring myself to throw away a full bottle that cost this much. As a hand soap, it is fine. The scent is lovely on my hands, and it does not dry out my hands the way it does my scalp.

If this product is the ultimate disappointment. A beautiful fragrance trapped in a formula that simply does not work for washing your hair. If the company sold this as a perfume only, I would buy it in a second. But as a shampoo, it is a waste of money. I cannot recommend it for actual hair washing unless you want to follow up with a bad hair day every time. Two stars for the scent, zero stars for performance. Buyer beware.

title: Great Book!
text:
I picked up "Great Book!" based on the title alone — yes, I was that curious. And honestly, for the most part, it lives up to its name. The writing style is engaging and conversational, which made it easy to get through in just a few sittings. The author covers some fascinating ideas, blending personal anecdotes with solid research in a way that never feels dry. I found myself highlighting several passages and even dog-earing a few pages to revisit later.

What keeps it from a full five stars for me is the pacing in the middle section. Around chapters four through six, the narrative loses a bit of steam. The concepts start to feel repetitive, and I wished the author had either tightened that part or introduced a fresh angle sooner. It picks back up nicely in the final chapters, but that middle lull took some effort to push through.

Also, a minor but noticeable issue: the paperback edition I received had a few smudged print lines in one chapter. Nothing unreadable, but slightly disappointing for a new book.

Overall, "Great Book!" is a solid, thought-provoking read that I’d recommend to anyone interested in the subject. Just be prepared for a brief slowdown before the strong finish. Worth the money, but not quite a flawless gem.

This story isn't just about love and loss, its about impossible choices and heartbreak. No matter what Mia's choice, she feels that she loses a piece of herself.

We follow Mia througout the book on a journey through her memories, making you better understand how badly she will break if she wakes up and has lost her family. We also see her relationship with Adam and how much they truly care about each other and how their lives are clearly drifting in different directions.This story is painful just to read but beautifully written and really hits its mark in making you sit at the edge of your seat to see which avenue she will choose.

title: Outstanding little pump at fair price/switch is questionable
text:
UPDATE: April 2016 -- I've been using this pump for a little over a year and the pump, itself, continues to function well but I'm beginning to have problems with the float switch. The switch now turns the pump on in the full off position but, if I raise it I/2 inch, it turns off. It will restart gain at about 1 1/2 inches up or floating. I've managed to keep it working by holding it above the full off position with a rope but I'm now concerned that the rope will float away and the pump will run until it burns up or destroys the battery by running it until it is totally discharged. It appears to find a quality float switch, I'll have to spend about as much for the switch as I have for the switch and pump combo and the add-on pump. I'm still very pleased with the pump. It does what it's supposed to and does it well.

This is a strong pump for its small size and low cost. It took about fifteen minutes to pump out a twelve foot Portabote that was three quarters full of water and it's worked without fail since I installed it to keep the boat rain water free. At just over $20 for the pump and switch with an additional backup pump as a $5 add-on, this is a super bargain. So far both pump and switch have proven to be reliable but they're not designed for heavy duty use and I would not think of using them in situations where the vessel will be unattended for a long period of time or when large volumes of water need to be dealt with. While the pump can clear a significant amount of water quickly, it's really designed for light incidental use. I'm very happy with this purchase because I believe that I'm using the pump and switch as they were intended...in a non-critical situation to handle incidental rainwater and spray. To ask them to do much more could be asking for trouble.

text:
I'm very happy with this cart, and two reasons stand out: its sturdiness and its size.

It's a very clever design, and the parts are of high quality. The result is a rigid structure that's perfect for applications like mine: support for a wide-carriage "pro" printer that can be placed on the top shelf without the somewhat massive printhead action causing side-to-side sway.

The size is a difficult one to find elsewhere. In my case I needed to replace a cheap TV cart made of low-density fiberboard and formica. I was using it to support not only the aforementoned wide printer on top but also a laser printer and scanner on the lower shelf. Any replacement would have to be almost the same size because of my office setup. I was ready to give up -- most shelving/carts like these are dimensioned in multiples of 12 inches -- but then I found this guy (the 16x28). Perfect! A little taller than the crumbling TV cart, but that's OK. I gained a third shelf for supplies that previously lived on the carpet under the cart.

One problem (for me): Carts like these have no sides onto which you can stick things -- in my case USB hubs. The solution was fairly simple: pegboard material cut to size, held in place with toggle bolts (with shortened screws).

One caution: unlike wood shelf units, which typically have uniform shelf width front to back, carts like these have tubing at the four corners that you might need to take into account. If your printer, for example, is a tight fit on one of the lower shelves, it might fit fine and work fine but not allow you to pull out the paper supply drawer if you can't skooch it over. The inner post-clearing distances for the shelves in this case is about 25.5 inches (left-to-right as pictured) and about 13.5 inches (front-to-back as pictured).

Regarding ease of assembly... Yes, the instructions are terse, but it's not rocket science. If you have a third-grader in the house, you should be fine.

All in all, a very satisfactory purchase and a good value.

title: Good noise suppression and durability for a fantastic price
text:
I bought these after looking through various first- and third-party solutions for low-noise Mavic Pro props. I'm using them on an original Mavic Pro (not a Platinum) and I absolutely love them for 3 reasons:

1, they make a big difference in terms of the Mavic's sound output. I haven't done formal tests with a decibel meter, but it's obvious that the flights are significantly quieter with these props both indoors and out. I now tend to have some trouble hearing my Mavic once it's up to about 150-200ft even when directly overhead (though obviously quick altitude changes or movements change that). It's made it much less obtrusive than the original props. I haven't tried other brands and therefore can't compare to other manufacturers' low-noise props, but you'll definitely notice a big improvement over the stock blades.

2, their durability seems just as good as the original props'. I read several reviews of other low-noise props that complained that the gold tips were made of a softer, more easily deformed plastic. That isn't the case with these, as it's the same material along the entire length. That may make a slight difference when it comes to aerodynamics, but it means I don't have to worry about them when folding up the props (by the way, they fold up just fine despite their slightly larger size, as long as you're a little careful when unfolding the back legs and don't get the pairs intertwined). The paint scuffs relatively easily, but that's it. I've replaced one set after stupidly crashing into some scrubby branches, but even then there were only a few minor nicks and gouges that I probably could have gotten away still flying with, but at this price it's stupid not to just get another set.

3, obviously the price is amazing. These are half the price of all other manufacturers' props that I could find, and at $8 for a complete set it's really hard to argue with when you get such significant noise reduction. I can't imagine going back to anything else. I'd buy 2 sets just to have some spares.

He showered them with gifts; traveled with them; and of course, financially helped them. He seemed particularly obsessed with the older boy, George. Barrie loved to photograph all of the boys and some of the photos included in this book show the children naked. Was Barrie a pedophile of sorts? None of the boys ever accused him of such. And Barrie's love and concern for the boys did not end when they became men who were tall enough to tower over the diminutive playwright.

This is a comprehensive look at Barrie's life without passing any judgement. That is left to the reader. And after reading this book, I have to say that I'm STILL unable to figure the man out. He is an enigma. There are tons of photographs - one or two on just about every page. Original correspondence and notes from Barrie's diary/journals add further insight. A fascinating, and sometimes tragic look back in time.

text:
I just received my first mommy calendar in the mail, and I have to say, I absolutely love it! It exceeded all of my expectations, not just in terms of design, but in functionality. The paper quality is also impressive. It feels thick and durable, which means I don’t have to worry about ink bleeding through to the next page, a common issue with cheaper notebooks. The binding is sturdy, allowing the calendar to lay flat on my nightstand or kitchen counter, which is incredibly convenient when I need to make a quick entry in the middle of the night or during a busy diaper change.

Beyond its practical features, the aesthetic appeal of the calendar brings a sense of joy to my daily routine. The soft, neutral tones are soothing to look at, and the overall design feels modern yet timeless. It doesn’t just sit there gathering dust; it becomes a cherished part of my daily life. I’ve already recommended it to several friends who have recently become parents, and I plan to buy another one as a gift for our upcoming baby shower. If you are looking for a meaningful way to document your journey into motherhood, I cannot recommend this product highly enough. It is a beautiful, functional, and heartfelt addition to any new parent’s home. title: Didn’t last a day
text:
I was genuinely excited to try this product after reading the glowing reviews and seeing the impressive marketing claims. It promised durability, comfort, and an easy setup process, which seemed like exactly what I needed for my energetic golden retriever. I spent the afternoon assembling it, following the instructions carefully, and everything seemed to fit together perfectly at first glance. It looked sturdy on my hardwood floors, and my dog gave it a quick sniff before ignoring it for a few hours. That quiet period, however, was short-lived. By the next morning, the structural integrity was already compromised. One of the main support legs had snapped right at the base, despite me not applying any excessive force or weight. I didn’t even have my two hundred-pound mastiff near it; it was just sitting there.

The plastic material feels cheap and brittle, not at all like the heavy-duty resin advertised in the description. When I tried to tighten the loose connections, the threads stripped completely, rendering the entire assembly useless. I reached out to customer support, expecting some level of assistance given the obvious defect, but was met with a generic email asking for more photos. It has been three days, and I still haven’t heard back. For a product at this price point, I expected at least a week of usage before any signs of wear, let alone catastrophic failure. It is incredibly frustrating to buy something that is supposed to make pet care easier, only to have it become another piece of clutter in my garage. I cannot recommend this to anyone who wants something reliable. Save your money and invest in a brand with a better reputation for quality control. My dog is currently happier with an old, worn-out toy that has lasted years, rather than this shiny new disaster that fell apart before I even finished my morning coffee.

A greater appreciation for this family and the hardships and sacrifices they had lived through in order to survive was unimaginable. title: More like "Helping Badger Overcome Depression"
text: I was surprised to see this book so breezily reviewed.  I myself found it disturbing.  There are lots of good books around that deal with bad moods--"Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Really Bad  Day" and "Today I Feel Silly & Other Moods That Make My  Day" come to mind.  This book goes way beyond moodiness and knocks on  the door of clinical depression.  First, the animals find Badger sitting in  his chair in the dark.  When they switch on the light, Badger snaps at them  to turn it off and leave him be.  The other animals leave, but Mole is  worried about Badger so he stays and cleans up the place a bit. Badger  eventually speaks: "I'm sorry about this. 'Spect I'll get over it.  But right now, I'm just no good, you know.  No good for anything."  Mole tells him they'll "just wait".  Eventually the animals call  a doctor.  Badger refuses to see her and sends Mole out to get rid of her  and the other animals trying to help:  "Close the curtains," he  begged Mole.  "Keep them away."  Then we have a scene where Mole  watches Badger "staring and dozing and turning heavily in his  chair."  YIKES! And then, just when you're sure Mole is going to be  calling the suicide hotline, things turn rosy and child-appropriate again.  Mole comes up with the idea of an Awards Ceremony (this causes Badger's  eyes to move "sharply for the first time in days").  Badger and  all the other animals attend.  Badger wins all sorts of awards for being a  good person/badger.  At last he feels "appreciated" and is happy.  Everyone dances.  I was confused (and creeped out).  My child was  confused:  "How come he wants to sit in the dark?...How come he  doesn't want the doctor to help him?...Doesn't he like the other animals  anymore?...Does he like them better now that they had a party for  him?"  If this had been a book to help children understand  depression--a book with an appropriate resolution and ending--it would have  been fine.  If this had been a book about a badger who was feeling glum and  unappreciated, who was then cheered up by an awards ceremony, it would have  been fine.  But this book is a bizarre marriage of the two and it is AWFUL.

title: Twisty Rods for Beachy Waves or Coily Curls
text:
My hair has lots of different kinds of curls in it, from tight coils near the nape of my neck, to spirals, all the way to slightly wavy hair at the crown of my head. I get a more consistent curl when I use curlers! I've been using large foam curlers for a while to get large, uniform waves that straighten out over a few days, but I wanted to try a curler that would give me tighter curls.

The Ohuhu Twist Flex Rods come with 7 different curl sizes, and each size has 6 rollers. The rollers are color-coded by size, so you think I'd be able to find all 7 curlers, but apparently I thought there were only 6 when I took the picture. I'd never used these kinds of curlers before, but they were simple to use. I used the two largest sizes, and took a small section of hair and put the end of it in the middle of a roller. Then, I rolled the hair up into the roller, making sure to keep the hair in the center of the rod. Twisting the ends together keeps the curler in place.

I tried to let my hair air-dry with the curlers in, but I have a LOT of hair, and knew that could take days, so after a few hours, I put on my bonnet dryer and finished the job. I was pretty happy with my ringlets! I did muss them up for a nice, beachy curly-wave, too. I really liked getting the curl all the way to my crown, and how much lift it gave the top of my 'do. And, the curls weren't tangly like my hair can get if I let it completely air dry. I could run my fingers through them and get a messy, beachy wave - and still no frizz or tangles.

(I received this product for review purposes. My opinions are my own. For more information and pictures, please see my blog, Lit From Within.)

title: Good, even-handed account of Davis' flight
text: The Long Surrender is a good book with the wrong title, because Jefferson Davis certainly did not surrender.  This book chronicles the events beginning in April of 1865, when Lee surrendered and Richmond fell.  Jefferson Davis and his entourage fled with the remaining treasury.  The author gives a well-researched and even-handed account of the flight of Davis.  It captures his determination to somehow rally the remaining forces and continue the war, despite the advice of his generals.  I bought this book because I wanted to understand Davis better and learn what is known about his postwar days.  It's a bit dry, but nevertheless interesting.  Davis spent two long and miserable years in confinement, and was treated inhumanely by his captors.  It recounts the anguish of his wife and her efforts to obtain at first better treatment and finally his release.  The book is chock full of little known facts about this dark period of history.  It gives a fairly detailed accounting of the Confederate treasury and the personal funds of Davis.  There is no glossing over the flaws in judgment and intransigent attitute of Jefferson Davis, but the book also illuminates his courage, conviction, and many good qualities.  For those who want to see the bitter end of his "presidency" this book is a must.

Marvel still had some great comics in the early '90s like Gruenwald's run on Captain America and Mark Bagley's artistry on Spider-Man, but this book was a sign of things to come as comic plot lines became so mixed up and convoluted that it hurt the industry so badly Marvel nearly went bankrupt.

The best and most effective Marvel superhero crossover is still the original 12-issue Secret Wars series, released in 1984 (and one that had the most lasting consequences, ie Spider-Man's black suit, the Thing leaving the Fantastic Four, etc). Infinity Gauntlet's worth a read, but fails to deliver in its promised scope, and certainly a tale that isn't, by any means, a pivotal moment in Marvel comicdom.

I am genuinely shocked that this product is still on the market with such a low rating that hasn't deterred buyers. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you need an air mattress, save your time and go buy a reputable brand from a well-known manufacturer. This item is essentially trash wrapped in plastic. title: horrible
text:
I held on to an old box of Swingline size 11 rubber fingers from 20 years ago, and started using them at work finally almost 2 years ago. I love them.

I just finally wore out the last one (I only had 6 to start with), and ordered these as replacements. They are horrible - not even remotely close to the original product. The rubber is stiffer, and harder, and thinner, and the size isn't even close to right. I ordered both size 11 & 11.5, because I recently ordered the Acco brand size 11 from Staples, and they were too small. These Swinglines are identical to the Acco brand from Staples - they are the same product, if anyone is wondering, except the size 11 I received from Amazon are even smaller, and the 11.5 are too big for my finger. Really - a half size varies so wildly that neither of them fit my index finger.

I am just going to assume that they are making them as cheap as humanly possible and have no desire to have any level of quality control, nor care about the comfort of their product. The rubber doesn't even have a tack to it, unlike the old ones I have. The new ones might not stretch out, but to me, that is not a plus. I would rather have a fingertip that stretches over time, but at least it works for several months of daily rigorous use before it finally wears out.

I must now search for another product that might suit my needs, or try to find an old box on ebay - which is always a gamble, and not a permanent solution.

I miss the old days wear quality mattered - I can't buy a children's game, or even a t-shirt - that has any quality craftsmanship about it. I'm really tired of cheap and crappy stuff.

What a waste of time. I'll keep limping along with my stretched out fingers as long as I can - or maybe I can gain 50 pounds, gets fat enough to fit inside the ones I have.

title: Not Indestructible, but a Great Value
text:
Our shiba loves these toys. For small dogs (20-25lbs), shibas are notoriously rough and tumble players, with the ability to tear through a cold turkey in a matter of minutes (or so one popular breeder/trainer attests from personal experience). So, imagine what they can do to their toys!

Our girl is relatively (key word, here!) calm for a shiba. She never touches anything that isn't hers, but she can get the crazies and do a number on her toys. Tug-of-war is her davorite game, after all, and these are made for it. So, the fact that these are stuffingless is reassuring. She will sometimes tear the ears off of the foxes, but it's from over-time wear-and-tear. She will eventually rip the giant one up (high-energy breeds of any size above a toy breed will need the jumbo), but it will last long enough to be worth the ten or so dollars.

Bottom line, I very much recommend these for all but the most destructive of dogs. The only reason I am not giving five stars is due to the fact that they do eventually wear down, but the low price makes this tolerable. The only other critique I have is that the animal you get seems random, with no visible way to request one over another (our girl really prefers the fox).

title: Wonderful Book - Looking forward to a 2nd Ed.
text:
Fr. Emmanuel does an admirable job of commenting on various liturgical questions, and does not balk at some of the more contentious issues (cf. "The Gate and the Curtain" pp. 181-2; who knew that St. John Chrysostom mentioned the use of a Curtain?!), providing multiple perspectives. It is set up as a textbook including multiple layers of depth in commentary, from the more casual student of Liturgy, to the more scholarly.

A second edition would be most welcome, as there are a number of page cross-references which are incorrect, and at least one diagram is mentioned which does not appear in the text. Much recourse in footnotes is made to electronic sources, which may simply be the direction of modern scholarship, but does evoke a double-take when used in a field that stretches back millennia.

In all, a wonderful start, and a second edition to take care of minor housekeeping issues will be most enthusiastically received.

Peter Maas recounts the remarkable story of the submarine, the USS Squalus, which sunk to the bottom of the North Atlantic in May of 1939. Charles "Swede" Momsen, a U.S. Navy officer, and a revolutionary scientist, was summoned to rescue these men from their watery grave.
Maas vividly depicts the tense moments involved in this heroic rescue. He uses a fast-paced language, peppered with an excellent combination of quotes and technological terms to create a very thrilling and riviting read. I almost felt as if I was part of the rescue operation myself.
Although this book kept me interested in its suspenseful voyage, the technical terms could have probably been described in a slightly more reader-friendly manner. I found myself a little confused at some times, but the overall flow of the book was still pretty smooth.
I enjoyed the epilogue quite a bit, as this small section is where the reader really gets to see the personal side of Momsen. This book was truly excellent. It was a pleasure to read. I could not put it down.

title: Alternative history strategy with a dash of random dice rolling
text:
As others have mentioned, Dust is like a beefed-up version of Risk where you can drop Mechanized Armor Units from the sky and send strategic bombers on a grand tour of alternate history WWII. It's fun, it's easy, and it requires just enough imagination and skill to keep you interested for hours.

The game itself comes with 2 rule books and about a million game pieces. The good news is, these pieces are actually kind of fun and more often than not you'll find yourself organizing units together as your opponent figures out his next move. Dust also comes with two different rule books, one for Premium and one for Epic. This is just shorthand for "long game" and "longer game". Along with these items, players also use cards to determine what types of moves they'll make and what special abilities they'll be able to bring into play with each turn.

If I only had one complaint with the game it's that it doesn't really capitalize on its theme all that much. Sure you get a great map of the apocalyptic future-scape, a ton of pieces representing everything from submarines to Mechs, and a card system that provides some pretty great artwork, but overall the whole idea of this "alternative history" World War II is all in your head. You don't really follow any stories, so most games end up being a large-scale RISK that doesn't suck as much as its predecessor.

All in all, I recommend this game for nothing else than being fun and entertaining.

title: Excellent narrative but questionable claims
text:
This is an excellent narrative history of contributors, ideas, movements, and events in German culture. Peter Watson communicates his encyclopaedic knowledge very readably. He summarises major thinkers and cultural movements concisely, but rigorously, with a great gift for succinct meaningful précis.

However, Watson’s claim that the extent of the German contribution to modernity is unique (eg page 828 on ‘The First XI of Modern History’ which includes Mendel!), is unsustainable. Roy Porter claims otherwise in his ‘Enlightenment: Britain and the Creation of the Modern World’ as does Sudhir Hazareesingh in ‘How the French Think’. It is in any case a claim which lends support to the objectionable idea of German superiority. Renaissance and Enlightenment were pan-European projects.

Watson’s interesting thesis is that Pietism, Bildung and Innerlichkeit account for the German genius, but he does not show how these qualities of individual worth and spirituality fit with a strong tendency to communal obedience in German culture. He does however show how nationalism was initially a liberal idea challenging the old illiberal autocratic feudal German states.

Watson does not cover the major contribution of church, particularly in post-war German society. The West German Protestant church established the bi-annual ‘Kirchentag’ movement dedicated to persuade the German Christian to follow individual conscience rather than state dictat, and to include the outsider. The East German church hosted the political reform movement that led to ‘die Wende’, although the East’s DDR resisted acknowledgement of Holocaust guilt for too long.

Watson has provided a mine of data for a fuller debate on the causal factors, the nature, and the extent of the German contribution.

Before we had gotten all the Deco bits taken off the plastic frames, the back panel had popped out of the frame. To restore it properly, several pieces had to be taken apart. The only way I could get the counter top to stay fastened to the base was to attach it with double-sided tape.

The set contains 135 pieces. A few pieces are decals. There are maybe 20 larger pieces. However, the rest are very small plastic pieces, the kind that small pets and toddlers choke on. The kind that children leave all over the floor and you step on in the middle of the night on your way to the bathroom or refrigerator. The kind you're still digging out from beneath the car seat when the child graduates from high school. Enough said?

In spite of my lack of enthusiasm for the Littlest Pets Shop Style Set, the 4 girls loved it. They happily played with everything. They set up the shop, decorated the side walls, the dog house, and the pets with the Deco Bits. They let the monkey swing from the chandelier and gave the pets new names. They just had fun. On their way out the door, the two older girls were asking their mom if they could go to the store. No one had to asked why...

text:

Assembly was minimal—just snapping on the treads and putting batteries in the shell. It is a fantastic gift option that offers genuine play value rather than just being a static display piece. If you are looking for a durable, engaging toy that brings the nostalgia of the cartoon to life, the Shellraiser is worth every penny. text:
I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays. I felt drunk on this book. I rarely underline or write in books, but I couldn't help myself with this one: Chew-Bose's writing is so unique, yet so relatable at the same time. She put to words feelings I've had—of being young, of being a woman, of the relationship you have with your parents—that I've never expressed, feelings and thoughts I didn't realize others shared too, that I now realize are possibly universal parts of growing up. I read, reread, wrote down passages, sighed after reading many more. I savored this book.

"Your hot friend on a balmy summer night telling you about some good news in her life is—how do I put this without sounding absurd? It's barometric. It's love and you love's power growing, and it's watching the elements cater to a woman who exudes."

"We are waking up to freckles dotting a person's back, and leveling that we might be in love—not with this person, but with freckles and downy morning light, because unfamiliar contours before 9 a.m. have a way. With someone new, even freckles become spotless. They are a surface blurred and time deferred. Everything begins simply enough."

I texted excerpts to friends, including the two above, and three asked to borrow it. Of course, I need to reread it a third time before I lend it out (I may just purchase a second copy). This book is a marvel—I can't wait to read what Chew-Bose writes next.

title: Hair needed a GOOD wash
text:
I purchased this item last month because my daughter has curly hair that tends to get quite tangled and dry after swimming at the local community pool. The product description claimed it was specifically designed to remove chlorine and salt buildup while maintaining the natural moisture barrier of the hair shaft. I was skeptical at first because there are so many shampoo bottles on the market with similar sounding benefits, but I decided to give it a try since the ratings were generally positive and the price point was reasonable compared to high-end salon brands.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the bottle was the scent. It is not overly floral or fruity, which I appreciate. It smells more like a fresh, clean ocean breeze with a hint of mint. It is refreshing and not overpowering, which is important because strong perfumes often linger in hair for days and can be headache-inducing for some people. I let my daughter wash her hair with this product twice a week for the past three weeks, and I have noticed a significant improvement in the manageability of her curls. They feel softer and the definition is much better than when I used our previous brand.

However, I am only giving it four stars instead of five because of the lather. It does not produce as much foam as I expected. For someone who is used to the heavy, dense bubbles from conventional shampoos, this might feel like it is not actually cleaning her hair. I had to apply a larger amount than I normally would to get the feeling of a thorough cleanse. It is not a dealbreaker, but it is something to be aware of. Additionally, while the bottle is durable, the pump mechanism is a bit stiff and requires a bit of pressure to dispense the product. It works, but it is not as smooth as I would like.

Overall, the performance is excellent. The hair feels genuinely clean without being stripped of natural oils, and the frizz has reduced noticeably. I think this is a solid choice for anyone looking for a gentle, effective wash that respects the integrity of curly or textured hair types. It does what it promises, even if the packaging and lather could be slightly better. I would recommend it to friends who struggle with dry, chlorinated hair, but perhaps suggest they start with a small amount to see how their hair reacts to the lower lather formula. It is a good product, just not perfect.

title: Sarah has a beautiful way with words
text:
The 411 by Maria:
I received this book right before Mother's Day. It is absolutely incredible. It is one perfect, powerful poem. A poem made into a book for mother's to give daughters and friends to give each other.

Having a daughter for me, was on my bucket list. I knew I didn't have much say in the matter and prayed for Goddess as hard as I could without going overboard afraid that if I begged too hard, God would feel it was unfair and unwarranted.

What Sarah Kay does is takes everything I have ever felt or thought about my daughter and put it into words. Every girl should have a copy of this book. They should read it and re-read it because Sarah speaks the truth. Life will hit you in the face and wait for you to get back up so it can kick you in the stomach. This is a healthy dose of reality but written in a poetic, joyful way, truly beautiful way.

Apologize when you've done something wrong. .
But don't you ever apologize for the way your eyes refuse
to stop shining; your voice is small,
But don't you ever stop singing.

That lines brings tears to my eyes. It is everything I would have wanted someone to say to me as a child and it exactly how I want my Goddess to grow up. Never ever stop singing.

After you read the book for the 10th time, go back and watch Sarah Kay read it. She really is very special and I want to thank her for writing everything I would want to say if I knew how.

title: I love this book!
text:
I really enjoyed reading this book! Mona, the main character, is easy to relate to...and she has red hair! Being a ginger myself, I have a special affinity toward ginger characters (we're under represented)! My bias aside though, Holden's writing style really brings the characters to life. They are realistic...their lives aren't spectacular, they don't have these amazing careers or live in a mansion. They are normal people, living in an average house, complete with a crotchedy old neighbor! I love it. It was so easy to relate to their lives and picture them as my own neighbors or somebody I would be friends with. I was really touched by Mona's rediscovery of herself and her husband. There is a lot of laughter in Becoming Mona Lisa too...Mona and her husband have witty, cynical, comical personalities and I found myself laughing quite a bit. I also found myself feeling all gushy over the rekindling romance between husband and wife.

Holden does such an amazing job of describing the surroundings that I feel I could draw a picture of the Siggs home! I can picture the mean old codger that lives across the street, the bird infestation, the mannequins, even the Walmart that Mona works at. Throughout reading this book, I was reminded of the reasons I love my fiance and what brought us together. I don't know if Holden intended this...but it definitely reminded me not to take him or our relationship for granted. The book flows really well and I definitely found myself wanting to read more after I finished. So I'm really hoping there's a sequel to Becoming Mona Lisa, because I really wanna follow the next chapter in Mona's life...and I REALLY wanna know what's up with the room! I definitely strongly recommend this book.

I bought this electronic device after reading several reviews and comparing specs with similar models. For the price point, it delivers solid performance overall, but there are a few areas that keep it from being a five-star product.

The app that controls the device is functional but a bit clunky. The equal to clunky. It takes a few seconds to load, and some settings are buried in menus. I wish they would simplify the interface. Also, the power button is a bit stiff requires a firm press.

For the money, this is a good product. It does what it supposed to do without any major issues. If you can live with the average battery life and a slightly clunky app, you will probably be happy. I would recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable device for everyday use and does not need top-of-the-line features. Four stars from me.

text:
POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD:

I honestly have to say that it's not only the best book I've ever read but probably one of the greatest pieces of writing I've ever read. From beginning to end, I found myself completely drawn to the story of Jersey City bus driver Andre Bolden.

The book is a real page turner and what really kept me hooked besides wanting to know the story resolution was the relationship between Andre and Sandra, the mother of his son. Sandra had so much resistance towards him that I kept turning pages eager to see if Andre could ever get over that emotional fortress. At the same time, the theme about snitching itself was handled very well by Mr. Mattison without being too imposing about it. Rather than making it about a guy or people around him who don't snitch, it comes across as a story of a man whose wrong choices in life start to eat him up bit by bit, living in the fear of losing his life as he had with getting kicked out of school, losing Sandra, and eventually losing his job. He thinks living back with Sandra and Little Dre would solve all his problems. But what transpires over the course of the book leads Andre to a much higher purpose of standing up for himself and those dearest to him.

I also want to applaud Mr. Mattison himself for being able to write the book using little to no profanity. I'm sure it was quite a challenge to do that given the genre and the tone of the book.

Overall, this is a must read for teenagers and adults across America. Look forward to the movie adaptation.

title: Look What I See
text:
This series entitled, "Look What I See! Where Can I Be?" which includes the previous titles that explored "the neighborhood", "the home", "my animal friends" and "visiting China", now examines "the synagogue" with mixed results. The publisher promotes the book as "exploring a week in Jewish family life", but that week constitutes a rather confused timeline for most adults familiar with Jewish rituals and traditions. The concept is one that is completely appropriate for very young children. An inquisitive toddler and her doll view items relating to Jewish rituals and then, with a turn of the page, we see her and her family photographed at the larger event. For instance, the text reads, "On Sunday, I fell asleep in my stroller. When I woke up, I saw a Kiddish cup." First we view the Kiddish cup in a clear photo, and then the toddler asks, "Where was I? By the Chuppah at a wedding." Within the wedding photo, clever toddlers will notice an apple and also the doll in his stroller. These photos and questions and answers are repeated 7 times for the days of the week and make for an appealing, structured format. However, this format does not work as well in a synagogue as it probably does for "exploring the neighborhood". Confusion abounds as we are led to believe that Rosh Hashana and Simchat Torah fall within the same week, or that apples are an integral part of every Jewish ritual. Confusion continues as the reader assumes the text to be the words of the toddler ("I fell asleep in my stroller"), but the photo then matches what the plastic doll is doing rather than the young girl. Also, the plastic doll, with a droopy, oversized blue kippah, is generally unappealing. Another issue involves the choice of photographs of both people and ritual objects. For example, the lulav is cut off, the dancers are blurry, and the "menorah" they chose to display is the stylized, artistic synagogue wall version, which is certainly not something a toddler would recognize from the home version. This book may work for some families comfortable with Reform traditions, but, in general, it needs to be revamped to appeal to its intended audience of Jewish families with small children.

Reviewed by Lisa Silverman

The final book of the Riders duology, and I’m happy with how it ended. Seeker by Veronica Rossi picks up where Riders left off. Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and Darryn and the remaining three horsemen will do anything to bring him back.

One thing that I don’t care for about this book is the romance. Not every story needs a love story, especially a story that’s so tightly focused on a group of friends. The romance didn’t add to the story and Darryn’s continuous pulling away from Gideon was exasperating by the middle of the book.

Cutting the romance out of the story, like Riders, it’s a very neat story with a unique point of view. The remaining horsemen are doing all they can to find Bass in The Rift. The Rift forces them to face their fears, and face their innermost demons.

Without giving much away, the journey to find Sebastian is one full of haunting memories and really learning more about the characters. I don’t feel like there was as much character development as their was in the previous book, but I don’t think that it’s really a bad thing with this book. I also wish that this book only had Darryn’s or only Gideon’s point of view, like the first book, and not bouncing between both.

I do wish there were more books in the series. Books from the other horsemen’s points of views would be interesting, and I’d definitely read them. All in all, a series that is enjoyable and provides a pretty unique premise for the characters.

Always in fear that around the corner of the next day, he was gone or dismissed as a composer, his only known livelihood. He felt that he could not achieve his best works. Other composers he knew who were in favor of the regime got fancy "prizes"/gifts of cars, housing, better foods. But he survived  even without those luxuries. title: A Funny Man Revealed
text:
I remember watching Steve Martin's seemingly meteoric rise from Tonight Show guest, to Saturday Night Live stalwart, to concert hall blockbuster. He made me laugh. He helped take the edge off the 70's. I remember leaving one of his Nassau Coliseum shows thinking that all in the world was good and it's ok to be goofy - for a little while anyway. It was from that melancholy recollection I read through this book.

While Martin's stand up humor was edgy, innovative, and visual, Born Standing Up is laced with a dry humor that sometimes brings chuckles one or two lines afterward. We can see that as is true for most seemingly overnight success stories there are years of hard work and sacrifice behind the sensation. Though there is only a small window into Steve's creative genius, you can see how his young life contributed to the product he presented on stage. Martin's stand up act was filled with silliness, idiocy, and just plain tomfoolery. In Born Standing Up we see the crafting of that act took an intellectual approach and technical dissection of how comedy works. Laced with stories of his family life, upstart employment, inspirations, encounters and collaborations with familiar performers from the era, and the eventual eruption of his show, Born Standing Up leads down a road of opportunities realized and acted upon.

Tracking the career of Steve Martin can be confusing. The performances of the stand up era are dramatically different from the ones we see in movies today. So different that when I played some of "Let's Get Small" for my kids (who are very familiar with the Cheaper by the Dozen dad) they had a hard time believing it is the same person. Born Standing Up reveals an underlying personality that is constant throughout Martin's career.

I believe this is a 5 star book for anyone who fondly remembers Martin's stand-up. Thanks Steve for making the world a little less serious!

title: When Simple Faith is Simply Not Enough
text:
"Today, twenty-first century theology tends to make religion a belief based upon faith rather than a belief of faith based upon fact. History, science, and conflicting Scriptures are all too often dismissed when they conflict with accepted creeds or dogma. Most Judeo-Christians are taught there are certain areas of their religion they should not question, causing the phrase “it is a matter of faith” to be well-worn and overused.
Scripture encourages individuals to question their idea of God."
And question it she did!
For Jodell Onstott, like so many of us, simple faith was simply not enough. Unable to dismiss the passionate; yet, conflicting views of countless denominations… the seemingly endless interpretations of a single text… the bearing of historic facts and archeological discoveries… the consequence of scientific evidences… Jodell embarked upon a decade long mission to discover the not so simple truth. And though the title of the subsequent book, “YHVH Exists” may eliminate the suspense of her ultimate conclusion, Jodell’s journey is a masterpiece of well-organized testimonies and closely examined proofs. Leaving no stone unturned, her systematic examination of the data demonstrates a sincere desire to reach an objective opinion.
The long-awaited “YHVH Exists” is a thorough and fascinating study that will challenge your most hidden preconceptions, and, may well find itself on the more than one bestseller’s list in the process.
Well worth the wait!
