title: I stayed up until 1:37 AM to finish this book
text:
I am not usually one to lose sleep over a paperback, but I found myself completely unable to put this book down last night. I had every intention of reading for thirty minutes before bed, but suddenly it was 1:37 AM, and I had reached the final chapter. That is when I know a book has truly succeeded in its mission to captivate the reader.

From the very first page, the narrative hook was undeniable. The author has a unique ability to weave complex characters into a plot that feels both urgent and intimately personal. I found myself relating deeply to the protagonist’s internal struggles, which are portrayed with such raw honesty that it felt like reading a diary entry rather than a novel. The pacing is relentless, yet never feels rushed. There are moments of quiet reflection that provide necessary breathing room, but the underlying tension never dissipates. It pulls you forward, chapter by chapter, with a momentum that makes putting the book down feel like a betrayal.

The prose itself is stunning. This isn’t just a story; it’s an experience. The descriptions are vivid without being overly verbose, allowing the imagination to fill in the gaps with crisp, clear imagery. I appreciated how the secondary characters were given distinct voices and motivations, avoiding the trap of becoming mere plot devices. They felt like real people with their own lives and agendas, which added layers of complexity to the main storyline.

What impressed me most, however, was the emotional payoff. I won’t spoil anything, but let’s just say the ending was both satisfying and heartbreaking. It stayed with me long after I closed the cover, prompting me to spend the next hour staring at the ceiling, processing the themes of loss and redemption. It’s rare to find a book that lingers in your mind days later, forcing you to re-evaluate your own perspectives.

For anyone on the fence, do yourself a favor and buy this copy. Whether you are a devoted fan of literary fiction or just looking for a gripping page-turner, this book delivers on all fronts. It is a masterclass in storytelling that respects the reader’s intelligence while delivering pure entertainment. I have already ordered a second copy as a gift for a friend who I know will have the same sleepless night I did. Five stars is not enough; if there were an option for six, I would choose it. This is that rare gem that reminds you why you fell in love with reading in the first place.

title: It's not about food
text:
Differently from the movie, this is not a tale about sophisticated food. It deals with the severe restrictions that puritanism imposes on pleasure - and how a tastefull dinner, with the help of some good wines, helps this fundamentalist lutheran aging community to retrieve joy and forgiveness.

In the movie, although the puritan restrictions are present, stress is on the food - the ingredients, the way it is being prepared, the discovery of it by the coachman and Bebette's assitant, and principally the precise description by the general. The transformation of the puritans, from mere tolerance of an extravagance to real appreciation and joy only underines the quality of what is being served.

In the novel, food plays a secondary role, contrasting with the grey sad environment and the equally gray and sad inhabitants of a norwegian community lost in the high north, squeezed between the mountains and an unfriendly see. Stress is on the way a severe pastor has molded the spirit of his daughters and of his few followers, banning all earthly pleasures.

I've decided to read the novel after having a dinner that reproduced the menu of Babette's feast, preceded by the film and a technical explanation by the danish chef. Dinner was excelent and our community did not resemble at all to the inhabitants of the small village - which in the film was moved from Norway to Denmark. I was first surprised by the differences in approach but then I realized that this short novel gives you food for thoughts. While the movie is pure pleasure, the novel is profound.

I recommend it and, if I may suggest, have it complete: the movie, the dinner and the short novel.

title: Game changer for walking my big dog
text:
My pup is a lab mix, about 80 pounds worth. She is crazy strong! She is very obedient everywhere but on a leash. Even with a rope slip harness around her neck she would get so excited that she pulled until her tongue hung out and my arm was sore.

This harness keeps her in check without choking or hurting her and I like it alot. It is easy to adjust and not visibly uncomfortable to her, never chokes her. She can eat or drink with it on. Walks are much easier. By controlling her head, her pulling is inhibited and she is more prone to listen to training commands. Squirrels or other dogs still get her excited and she will pull initially but if I use a shorter grip on the leash, she obeys. When we walk and she starts to tug, I stop walking and she relents. Pulling is never zero, but it is much more brief.

Others wrote that dogs can get the harness off and yes, if I don't pay attention she has tried to push it off her nose with her paw. A little correction stops that and we continue our walks.

It doesn't appear uncomfortable but she would prefer not to have any leash on of course. I only use the trainer on a leash, she doesn't wear it all the time and when I bring out the leash for walk time, she sits and waits to get it on. I tried a pinch collar in the past, she was definitely unwillingly to have that put on and would run to her kennel instead. Contrarily, she is eager to get this harness on and go for a walk anytime.

Walks are pleasurable again and we use it daily. Highly recommend.

text:
I have never before read a book where the author is so shamelessly self-promoting as Chris Brownfield. As another reviewer previously pointed out, his arrogance removes most (if not all) of his credibility, and makes this book very difficult to enjoy. For someone who was clearly not an outstanding JO (not by a long shot), he has way too much criticism and not enough respect for his fellow Navy submariners.

For a book titled "My Nuclear Family", Brownfield spends a lot of time talking about his IA in Iraq and his problems with the US government and the War on Terror. All organizations, particularly the US government has it's fair share of problems, however I hardly consider a sub JO an expert on politics or the intricacies of war. His claims that submarines are obsolete in today's Navy only further demonstrate his ignorance on the subjects.

I was led to read this book because I am quite familiar with the Navy's nuclear training pipeline and the job requirements of a submarine JO. As such, I was most interested in the first part of Brownfield's book which focuses on his time as a JO on the USS Hartford. It seems to me that Brownfield was a sub-standard officer at best, and is now a disgruntled ex-employee of the Navy who wanted to write a bitch-fest about how difficult his job had been while simultaneously making himself out to be the lone person deserving of respect in a profession he believes to be fallen.

I wouldn't recommend this book to anyone. The officers currently serving in our sub force are an important part of our national defense and are very deserving of our respect and gratitude, despite what Brownfield thinks.

text: First off, knowing how to play the basic triads for the the 4 primary scales, major, harmonic major, harmonic minor and melodic minor in 4 string groups is a helpful instigator of original ideas. The inversions that skip strings sound even better. I like the inversions using the two forms on the first 5 strings, Vic prefers strings 6,4 and 3. Then you are given moveable roots to go along with these triad inversions that give mini alteration flavor. Next up are traditional 4 note chords and their inversions of which you must learn the most common alterations.  Vic then goes into areas of stacked triad and modal harmony which give the book it's 'advanced' rating, Fascinating stuff for sure. To come up with these ideas and relationships on your own would be very tuff unless you were an unrelenting genius with resources. He concludes with chord charts of various voicings that include open strings . There is tab but it's only used to clarify suggested fingerings. To get the most out of this book you would need to be a student of music but there's nothing stuffy or drawn out about the presentation. He points out useful scalic relationships for the modal chord forms and many musical examples of the concepts presented. It seems more essential theory than White Elephant Theory . I'd take this one with me to a desert island because many musical questions are answered pragmatically and unselfishlessly. (My brothers phone is as funny as it is annoying). Key strokes are clean, clear, and instant. Alt, shift, Ctrl, and other hold buttons work exactly as you would expect them to. title: Very nice looking trash can
text:
When did garbage cans get so expensive?!?! I remember when I got my first home 10 years ago buying a really nice metal garbage can for $45 bucks….that being said, this Rubbermaid elite stainless steel garbage can is really nice!

The stainless steel finish is very aesthetically pleasing. Much better than any plastic trash can would look. I wouldn’t call the stainless steel fingerprint resistant like try yet claim, but it is super easy to wipe down. I usually just use a Clorox wipe and it looks as good as new.

The part that you step on is a good size and easy to use, and the lid pops open instantly when you step on it. No waiting for 5 seconds for it to open up like my old one. The lid also closes nice and slow and doesn’t make a peep when it’s closing.

There’s a little plastic switch on the inside that you can slide to make the lid stay open until you slide the switch back which is really convenient. It’s something really simple but it’s the first trash can I have had that did that and I really like it!

I try to recycle as much as I can, but I’ll admit there’s quite a few times that I throw plastic bottles away since my recycling can was in the basement. This makes it so much easier! I do still think the price is crazy high for a trash can, but it is competitively priced compared to other similar ones, so I can’t complain that much. Overall though I’m happy with it! Hopefully it will let a long time!

text:
I bought this for my seven-year-old’s birthday, thinking it would be a fun afternoon project we could do together. Several steps are ambiguous, and there is no indication of which side is up or which piece goes where until you’ve already forced something in the wrong direction.

I am not a stranger to putting together toys and furniture, but this one tested my patience. Some of the plastic connectors required a lot of pressure to snap into place, and I was genuinely worried I would break a tab. There are also small pieces that need to be inserted at just the right angle, and if you miss, the adult, miss that angle, the whole thing refuses to click. I ended up redoing three steps because I thought I had it right the first time. It took nearly two hours, whereas the box implied about 30 minutes. 

For the price, I expected a smoother experience. Once assembled, my child loves playing with it, but I would not buy this again for someone who does not enjoy a lot of spare time or patience. The design is clever design is undermined by the frustrating build. Three stars because the end result is decent, but the fun I expected, but the journey to get there was a two-hour headache that I could have done without. title: Sweet, slow, sad
text:
Thin Wood Walls follows young Joe Hanada's family experiences during the time of WWII. After the bombing of Pearl Harbor, Joe's father is taken away by the FBI as a person of suspicion because he is a community leader. The rest of the family, including Joe's feisty grandmother and more feisty big brother Mike, are taken to Tule Lake Relocation Camp and must adjust to a new life while anxiously awaiting the return of the father.

Not much happens in the book, as camp life is boredom, waiting, hoping, but Joe tries to make do and make sense of what is happening while fearing what his big brother intends to do. The story is balanced, showing how not all white Americans were against the Japanese in the U.S. Some Japanese were very angry while many exhibited a sad stoicism. Perhaps what sets this book apart from other internment stories is that it is set in the Tule Lake camp, which was where troublemakers, the "no-no's" and those wanting to return to Japan were sent. This created a turbulent, sometimes dangerous atmosphere that other camps did not experience, at least not on that level. Thin Wood Walls delves into this in a manner suitable for middle-graders.

The book is a bit slow, but sweet, the writing rather plain despite the bits of haiku, but this will appeal to boys as well as girls and provide a thoughtful look at the sad facts of this long-hidden part of U.S. history. Expect a tear at the end, and be sure to read the Author's Notes.

[[ASIN:0939165538 Looking Like the Enemy: My Story of Imprisonment in Japanese American Internment Camps]] is also set in Tule Lake, but is a true story. A Young Reader's edition is coming out in Fall 2010.

title: Pictures without much explanation
text:
I have a lot of ambivalence about this book. In some respects I'd give this 1 star and others i'd give it 5, so I split the difference and gave it 3 stars.
the good: The photographs themselves. You can see 2 examples of a scene and how Sam handled them differently.
the bad: I found the writing incomplete. It was like the attitude was, "Isn't it obvious? The photos speak for themselves!" and I don't think they do.
In some cases I thought both pictures were great and couldn't figure out which one was supposed to be better. In other cases I wondered, "What are people seeing? What makes this great?" and I found no help from the book.

After getting the book I saw a lecture by Sam on YouTube. It was about an hour long and he had many of the same photos in it. But in the lecture he explained what his goal was, what his approach was and why the final photo was the one he liked best. I thought this would have been great info to include in the book and wonder why it was not there. (OK, maybe it is obvious to everyone else in the universe and I just didn't get it. Totally possible, but I do have a strong visual arts background...but photography seems to play be different rules and it was not clear from this book what they are).

With Sam's lecture in my mind I like the book a lot better. But it seems odd that it did not work as a stand alone item. (at least for me, who had no experience with his working methods and goals when I first got the book).

Would I recommend buying it? Yes. But with the caveat of watching some YouTube lectures by Sam, if you are not familiar with his work and what makes it great.

title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

title: The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age
text:
I don't lightly rate books "I love it", but in The Connected Educator, Sheryl Nussbaum-Beach and Lani Ritter Hall practice the connected learning and leading of which they speak.

Prior to reading this book, I had been becoming a connected educator for almost two years. Then I found Sheryl and Lani hosting this book in a book study for Connected Educator Month, 2012. I joined in the study as much as I was able, since it was the start of a new school year, but watching them at work connecting and learning with those in the community cemented the learning for me.

The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age is a great book for wherever you are in digital age learning. Chapter 5 is a mini encyclopedia the basic web tools you should use and why to use them. In addition, I believe it is imperative for present and future principals to read Chapter 8, "Transforming Leadership for a Connected World."

Overall, I understood more deeply the philosophy of learning and leadership behind much of what I was learning to do. Now I am more committed than ever to learning and leading in the digital age.

Thanks, Sheryl and Lani.

title: Great game at a reasonable price
text:
I’ll be honest, I was a bit hesitant to purchase this game initially. I had seen a few other options on the market that promised similar mechanics but were significantly more expensive, and I didn’t want to spend a fortune just to see if my family would actually enjoy it. However, after reading some of the positive feedback and seeing the reasonable price tag, I decided to take the plunge. I am so glad I did, because this product has completely exceeded my expectations in almost every way.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the box was the quality of the components. The pieces feel sturdy and well-made, not flimsy like some cheaper alternatives I have tried in the past. The cards are thick and durable, which is crucial for a game that will be played repeatedly. The board itself is vibrant and clearly printed, making it easy to read even from across the table. It’s these small details that often make or break a gaming experience, and here, they are handled perfectly.

We played our first session last weekend with some friends, and the learning curve was surprisingly gentle. The rules are explained clearly in the manual, and we were up and running within ten minutes. The gameplay is engaging and strategic without being overly complicated. It struck a nice balance between casual fun and tactical depth, which meant that both the competitive gamer in our group and the more laid-back players felt included and entertained. There were plenty of moments of laughter and friendly debate, which is exactly what I look for when gathering people together.

For the price point, this is an absolute steal. I have played games that cost three times as much that were not nearly as fun or well-designed. This game offers tremendous value for money. It is versatile enough to be played with small groups or larger parties, and the replayability factor is high because no two games seem to play out exactly the same way. If you are on the fence about buying this, do not hesitate. It is a fantastic addition to any game night collection, offering hours of entertainment without breaking the bank. I have already recommended it to several other friends and family members, and I anticipate buying a second copy for my parents soon. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a fun, high-quality game that fits within a reasonable budget.

title: Well written kidnapping story that will keep you guessing.

Amy Gentry's novel, GOOD AS GONE, shares a lot of its plot with other movies and books. It also shares similarities with the true story of the kidnapping of Elizabeth Smart, from her bedroom at night.

A good portion of the story deals with the fallout that is created in the remaining family members when a child goes missing. The part that is similar to other works of fiction deals with how the family copes, when the hoped for miracle happens: the child returns to the family many years later, eliciting both joy and suspicion. The suspicion is driven by thoughts that the returning child (unrecognizable, after so many years) may, in fact, be an imposter.

text:
I bought this for my three-year-old, who is obsessed with stickers but tends to lose focus with more complicated craft kits. "More Lets Sticker and Paste" has been a fantastic addition to our quiet-time rotation. The book arrived in great condition, with sturdy pages that can withstand a bit of enthusiastic peeling and repositioning. What I appreciate most ishike most is the balance between open-ended creativity and gentle guidance. Each spread presents a simple scene—a garden, a kitchen, a fish tank—and provides a set of stickers and cutout shapes that your child can place however they like, but with enough structure that they don't get overwhelmed.

My son spent a solid thirty minutes on the first page alone, meticulously moving a frog from a lily pad to a flower, then back again. The paste portion is equally engaging. The book includes perforated paper pieces that you can tear out, and we used a basic glue stick to attach them. It is messier than stickers, but the activity encourages fine motor skills and planning: where does the apple go on the tree? Should the bird be in the sky or on the ground? The instructions are minimal, which I appreciate because it lets my child lead.

One thing that surprised me is how much we talk during these activities. He narrates what he is doing, and I ask questions about his choices. It feels less like a workbook and more like a shared experience. The book is also thick enough to last through many sessions. We have used about half the pages in two weeks, and the remaining ones are still crisp. I have already ordered another for a friend's birthday. If you have a toddler or preschooler who loves hands-on play, this is a no-brainer. It is screen-free, low-prep, and genuinely fun for both of us. Highly recommend.

It also has a convenient slot on the inside for your ID or Credit Cards, not to mention the belt holster for using the Zune on the go. The only negative I can possibly think of, is the access to the Play and Back buttons. Because of the thickness of the case, the cutout for the buttons is a little high off of the Zune's skin, so you'll have to dig in a bit deep to press the buttons. It's a minor inconvenience, something of a trade off for the superb protection this case provides. People with big fingers may want to take notice though. I would absolutely recommend this case to any Zune user. It offers excellent protection, great convenience, and a sleek, sporty look without too many weird straps and holes. I love it, and I'll bet you'd love it too. Definitely worth a try!

title: A real treat to Adrien and Jake fans, and a love letter from Josh Lanyon to these beloved characters.
text:
A very entertaining, thought-provoking, occasionally emotional read.

Fatal Shadows, the first book in the Adrien English series, being so well known to Josh’s readers, seemed like the perfect choice for a Choose Your Own Adventure version, because the characters and their original trajectory are so familiar that it becomes easy for readers to experiment with and explore even the wildest alternative scenarios,
The book also presents some new characters and some unexpectedly tender moments involving them,
Moreoever, some of the most satisfying storylines in this book are IMO those where a little more is subtly revealed of a character’s emotion and thought than in the original book. It has a liberating effect, as the CYOA concept allows a lot of freedom to uncover all those fears or bottled up emotions that in the original Fatal Shadows had remained under the surface,
The illustrations by Catherine Dair are the icing on the cake :). They make the book richer (and only a print edition could do them justice) and it’s a nice nod to the original CYOA book format which includes illustrations. And they’re not just there for decoration: Josh uses them as a plot device, so they can’t definitely be missed :)

All in all, I didn't expect such a rich and inventive book. What I did expect, and was not disappointed with, was the apparently effortless way Josh Lanyon has to combine humour, dry wit and emotion in such a creative and satisfying way.

title: Authentic characters make this a charming series starter
text:
I love how Austin's stories all knit together within the same small town community! You don't have to have read the other books in the series to enjoy each one individually, but by reading them all you get a fuller picture and more background on each of the characters. This start to the Bonfire Boys is a perfect example, taking minor characters from her other Love on Main series and putting them front and center.

Wild horses was a lot of fun, with city-girl-goes-country vibes. I loved Theron's inner battle and his relationship with his mother hits an unexpectedly heart-wrenching crux near the end. I didn't expect such a real moment in a romance novel, so it was a delightful surprise.

Skye is a satisfyingly believable character, with childhood damage and a lot of self-esteem issues. The way Austin describes her approach to and opinion of her paintings is incredibly accurate and gives the story an authenticity that many romance novels lack. Skye also gets her own personal wins that are unrelated to the romance, making you root for her even more. This (in addition to the sense of tight-knit small town community and over-protective family members) helps set a relatable stage full of players the reader can identify with.

Age gap usually isn't my thing, but this one worked fine for me. Skye is far more mature than her age. I enjoyed the self-conscious girl meets worshipping boy and city-vs-country tropes more. Theron has just the right amount of alpha-hole attitude and the steam is top notch. Looking forward to more in this series!

text: I am absolutely horrified and disgusted by how useless this product is. I cannot believe I actually took the time to write a review, because usually I am too tired to deal with these failures, but this situation is just too egregious to ignore. I bought this item specifically because my dog, Barnaby, has had severe anxiety issues for the past three years. We have tried everything. We have tried the prescription medications that made him lethargic and unkempt. We have tried the expensive, heated orthopedic beds that he refused to sleep on anyway. We have tried the calming sprays that smelled like expired lemon pledge and just confused him. This product was the last hope before I actually had to start carrying sedatives in my pocket every time I took him to the vet or the park. The marketing promised "instant results," "professional-grade tranquility," and "peace of mind for both pet and owner." Let me assure you, there was none of that. There was not even one percent of that. I set it up exactly as the instructions said. I turned the dial to the highest setting. I waited. I watched him closely for any sign of relaxation, for his breathing to slow down, for his ears to stop twitching at the sound of a leaf falling outside. Nothing happened. He sniffed it for approximately three seconds, looked at me with what I can only describe as pure judgment, and then proceeded to bark at a squirrel for another forty-five minutes. It was the same bark he has been doing since 2019. The noise was not dampened. The anxiety was not alleviated. I even held the device near his face, just to see if there was some magical ingredient or frequency I was missing. He sneezed. That was it. A single, annoyed sneeze. I am now out fifty dollars for a piece of plastic that does absolutely nothing. It is a light-up paperweight at best. I feel cheated. I feel like the company is running a scam on desperate pet owners who just want their animals to be happy. Do not waste your money. Do not waste your time. Save your cash and buy Barnaby a really good treat instead, because that will at least make him forget his anxiety for a brief second, which this garbage failed to do for even a fraction of a millisecond. I am returning this immediately. I hope the seller charges me a restocking fee, though honestly, I would pay them to take it back and destroy it so it never harms another pet owner’s wallet again.

title: Filled My Soul
text:
It was a privilege to read this book. The writing was bracing and the experience harrowing. By all rights, as awful as many of her trail experiences were, it could and should have been even worse.

To me, this book is a powerful reminder about the importance of taking on the near-impossible task/experience and facing down one's demons.
It is the journey of the hero, but told by a woman who felt like anything but when she set out.
Yes, she was horribly underprepared to trek the PCT and it was nuts to do it solo, and some of the confident hikers who commented scathingly can't forgive her that.
People who hate Elisabeth Gilbert of Eat, Pray, Love for leaving her perfectly sweet husband to "find herself" abroad will probably hate Cheryl Strayed for similar crimes, including self-indulgence.

But I found this a very powerful book. One that I expect to be thinking about for many years. One that I expect, and hope, will influence my own life.

The main reason I’m giving four stars instead giving four stars is that the compartments. I love that it has three sections, but they are a bit narrow. Also, the non-slip feet work well, but the base does wobble slightly on my counter if I bump it – not a dealbreaker, just something to be aware of. Overall, it’s a good value for the price. Looks good on the counter (no pun intended) and keeps my daily essentials handy. It’s just not as versatile as I hoped for larger containers. title: Birthday gift
text:
I purchased this item as a birthday present for my nephew, who is an avid cyclist and spends most of his weekends on local trails. The packaging arrived in decent condition, with no obvious damage to the box, which was a relief. However, once I opened it to inspect the product itself, I noticed several issues that have left me feeling somewhat indifferent about the overall quality. The material feels thinner than what was advertised, and upon closer inspection, I spotted minor stitching irregularities along the seams. While these defects do not immediately compromise the structural integrity, they certainly raise questions about the product's long-term durability, especially given that it is marketed for rugged outdoor use.

The design is undeniably sleek, and the color options are vibrant, which is why my nephew was initially excited when he opened it. He appreciated the multiple compartments and the water-resistant claim, which seemed practical for his needs. That said, after using it for just two short trips, the zipper began to stick occasionally, requiring some effort to close properly. This is a frustrating issue for a product at this price point, as convenience is a primary selling point for gear used in active lifestyles. Furthermore, the adjustable straps, while functional, feel slightly flimsy and do not secure as tightly as I would expect, leading to a bit of shifting when the bag is fully loaded.

On the positive side, the delivery was prompt, and the customer service team was responsive when I inquired about the warranty terms. It is clear that the brand puts effort into marketing and logistics, but the manufacturing execution leaves something to be desired. I cannot in good conscience recommend this as a top-tier choice for serious outdoor enthusiasts, but for casual use or as a secondary accessory, it might suffice. For the price, I expected a more robust build quality that could withstand regular wear and tear without showing signs of strain so quickly. It is not a bad product by any means, but it does not fully deliver on its promises of durability and ease of use. I hope future iterations improve the stitching and hardware quality, as the current model feels like a cost-cutting measure rather than a genuine upgrade for sports and outdoor activities.

title: Should be called a ‘wet bag’
text:
I am absolutely disgusted with this purchase and feel completely misled by the product description. I bought this item expecting a high-quality, waterproof container for my sports gear, specifically for carrying sweaty towels and damp clothing after intense workouts. Instead, what arrived in the mail is a pathetic excuse for a bag that does exactly what it should not: it leaks. Calling this a proper storage solution is a joke; it should honestly be classified as a "wet bag" in the worst possible sense of the term, meaning it is useless for its primary intended purpose.

The material feels incredibly cheap and flimsy from the moment you take it out of the package. It lacks any structural integrity, making it difficult to stand up on its own, which is a basic requirement for a gym bag. More importantly, the stitching along the seams is incredibly poor. I only used it once, for about thirty minutes while carrying a slightly damp towel and a change of clothes, and by the time I reached my car, water had seeped through the bottom and wet the entire contents of my other bags. This is not just a minor flaw; it is a complete design failure.

Furthermore, the zipper is a nightmare. It constantly gets stuck, requiring a level of patience and force that I never expected to exert on a simple accessory. Halfway through my walk home, the zipper slid down on its own, spilling wet laundry all over the pavement. This is humiliating and inconvenient. I tried to contact the seller to request a refund, citing the obvious defects, but they have been completely unresponsive. It is frustrating to spend money on a product that feels like it was thrown together in a factory with no quality control whatsoever.

Do not waste your hard-earned money on this item. There are countless better alternatives available at the same price point that actually offer true water resistance and durability. I am left with a soggy mess and a bag that is now too damaged to use for even dry storage. If you value your time and your belongings, steer clear of this product. It is not worth the hassle, the disappointment, or the additional cost of cleaning up the mess it inevitably creates. I am giving this one star because it is the minimum allowed, and honestly, if I could give zero stars, I would. The product is fundamentally broken and fails to meet the most basic expectations of a functional sports accessory.

As the host of The Wired Educator Podcast and the Director of Innovation and Instruction for Port Clinton Schools, it has always been my primary mission to celebrate and promote the voices of outstanding educators. The Wired Educator Motto is, “To Level Up and Make a Difference in the Lives of Students”. Keven’s book does that and more. Keven’s book emphasizes that students should be using devices to create MORE than they consume. I love the possibilities and direction Keven offers teachers to bring 3D printing to every grade and every content area.
It gives me great pride to help a fellow educator publish a physical book that another educator can hold in their hands, apply in their classroom, add to and pass along to others.
This is the first book published by Wired Educator. As I add these final words to this manuscript: I can feel the impact this book will have in students’ lives, I can picture the amazing creations students will design and produce, I can hear the laughs of failed prints, and the cheers of success as students and teachers collaborate together to create an environment of learning where experimentation, reflection on failure, and the tenacity to try again until they succeed is the norm.
Congratulations Keven on an amazing book and making a global impact on education. Well done.
Kelly Croy

This one is nice, but it is only pretty good compared to the one that doesn't put pressure on my eyes (Sleep Mask by Bedtime Bliss).

A warning: Don't tighten the mask too tight over your eyes! I wore this once recently during the day for a nap. I was worried about light, so I tightened the velcro a bit more than usual. I didn't think it was really tight at all, but I guess it was: when I woke up after an hour, my eyesight was blurry--even with my glasses on. Since strange things like this are sometimes normal if I wake during the wrong part of the sleep OR take a long nap too late in the day, I assumed it would pass. It took about an hour for the effects to wear off, and I was freaking out a bit the whole time. It wasn't until later that day when I remembered I had tightened the mask a lot more than I usually do. I'd hate to think what my eyes would feel like after a whole night if I had it tightened too much.

title: ... a few weeks and the coating on it became dull. If you splash a little soapy water on ...
text:
I really wanted to love this product because it looked fantastic right out of the box. The initial quality seemed high, and the finish had a beautiful, high-end shine that made my vanity look much more organized and elegant. For the first ten days, I was genuinely impressed with how it performed and how it looked in my bathroom.

However, after using it for a few weeks, the coating on it became dull. I noticed that the luster started to fade, and it developed a cloudy appearance that makes it look much cheaper than it did originally. I have been very careful with how I handle it, but the degradation happened surprisingly quickly. 

The most frustrating part is how difficult it is to maintain. If you splash a little soapy water on the surface, it doesn't just wipe away cleanly. Instead, it seems to leave a residue or a streak that is hard to buff out without further scrubbing, which I worry will only make the coating wear off faster. I tried using a microfiber cloth and a gentle cleaner, but the original radiance just isn't coming back.

It is a decent piece in terms of size and basic functionality, and it serves its purpose for holding my beauty products, but the durability of the finish is disappointing. I expected it to hold up better in a bathroom environment where moisture is common. For the price I paid, I expected the exterior to stay polished for more than a month. It is a three-star product for me because it works, but the aesthetic quality is lacking long-term durability. If you are looking for something that stays shiny and looks brand new, you might want to look for a different material.

title: Read THE TAMING before this one...
text:
PREQUEL: THE TAMING
Awww now. Once again this book reminded of why I have Jude Deveraux's name in one of my top 3 favorite author list. She is definitely gifted with words and know how to implement her very own heart soaring ideas. The lovable characters, the intriguing plot from the prequel of this book, THE TAMING, continues here in THE CONQUEST with much added exciting twist and some newly introduce charming characters.
There's 3 reasons why I didn't rate this book a fiver. One is because of the speedy conclusion of this wondeful SAGA. It was rushed and seemed uncomplete for me. Perhaps there is another book in the making to explain this kind of ending.... but if there's none, then I am sorely disappointed. I wanted at least an EPILOGUE with confirmation of decisions and etc. or a short extension of all the character's whereabouts and future. You'll know why and what I mean once u read THE TAMING and THE CONQUEST.
Two, I also wished Severn have his own story. I was not satisfied with his short-add-on story here in THE CONQUEST. Lady Anne is indeed a great match for Severn and I really would love to read more of them. I also would have enjoyed reading Iolanthe's appearance in Lady Anne and Severn's life. Again, you'll need to read THE TAMING and THE CONQUEST to know what I mean.
Third, I also would have love to see people's reaction to Zared's transformation from the BOY squire to a Lady. What of Ralph and Colbrand? Wouldn't it be fun to read their reaction?
Despite that three complains of mine, this book still manage to be a 4 stars to me because it did bring out lots of emotional helter-skelter in me... I love the way Tearle reaches out to Zared. His ways of courtship and his gentleness towards her. I sighed for Zared cuz I can see through her heart and understand her desires and confusions. The long awaited answers to the puzzles and mystery is not to be missed... but most of all, this book made me laugh. It's a grand book links.... Read to know what I mean!

title: Tineco soft roller
text:
I bought the Tineco soft roller vacuum expecting a premium experience given the brand’s reputation and the high price tag, but I have been thoroughly disappointed from day one. The main issue is that the soft roller collects pet hair exceptionally poorly, which was my primary reason for purchasing this specific model. Instead of wrapping around the hair, it seems to push it through or just spread it around the floor, leaving behind a frustrating mess that I have to clean up with a separate brush afterward. This completely defeats the purpose of buying a vacuum marketed for pet owners.

Furthermore, the battery life is nowhere near what is advertised. I have a modest-sized apartment, yet I cannot clean my entire home on a single charge without the battery draining much faster than expected. I have tried every cleaning cycle and even reset the device, but the performance has not improved at all. The customer support team was unhelpful and simply suggested I buy replacement filters, which feels like a dismissive way to handle what seems to be a fundamental design flaw in how the vacuum handles debris. For this premium price point, I expected reliability and effective cleaning power, not constant troubleshooting and subpar results. I’ve already started looking for a refund or an exchange, but I’m starting to lose hope. If you are on the fence, save your money and look elsewhere. This product is not worth the investment, as it fails to perform its most basic function efficiently and leaves you more frustrated than when you started.

title: Nice Cabinet and Board, BAD Darts
text:
I really wanted to love this set because, at first glance, it looks like a great value for the money. The cabinet is actually quite sturdy and looks professional once it is mounted on the wall. It does a good job of protecting the board and keeping the room organized. The dartboard itself is also decent; the sisal is tight, the numbers are clear, and it feels like it will hold up to a lot of play over the next few years.

However, the darts included with the set are a complete disappointment. I understand that this is a budget-friendly bundle, but these darts are almost unusable. The tips are inconsistent, and the flights are made of a cheap plastic that curls or tears after just a few throws. More importantly, the balance is completely off. I found myself struggling to hit basic targets, not because of my skill, but because the darts wobble mid-air. They feel lightweight and cheap, almost like toys you would find in a carnival game rather than actual sporting equipment.

If you are buying this for a game room or a garage, be prepared to spend an extra twenty or thirty dollars immediately to buy a proper set of brass or tungsten darts. I ended up using an old set I had in the attic, and the difference in performance was night and day.

In short, the hardware is great, but the accessories are garbage. I am giving this three stars because the cabinet and board are high quality enough to justify the price, but the inclusion of such poor-quality darts is a major letdown. It is a good foundation for a home setup, but do not rely on the darts that come in the box. Buy the set for the board, and buy your darts elsewhere.

The chief delight of this book, and there are many, is that Cunningham has tailored a page-turning, oh-no-don't-do-that!, classic plot of confused identity (i.e. a Comedy of Errors) onto a cutting-edge New York scene, and delivered it with humor, humanity, and depth in a style that is fashionable, highly entertaining, and sexy on the one hand, and deeply poetic on the other, as in he has maybe been reading not only the Bard but that other bard, James Merrill. The characters are sharply drawn both in body and mind, and the plot twists true to both life and character.
Other reviewers are complaining about over-writing. While this may be a bit like grousing that chocolate is rich, Cunningham does stumble here and there, e.g. when he has his hero/narrator say, 'What did Shakespeare say? Our little lives are rounded by a sleep.' This is artificial; Shakespeare himself would have solved the problem by giving that line to the college-student daughter, maybe upon seeing her father drinking vodka in the night!

title: Perfect OEM Replacement (+ install instructions) for Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
text:
Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
100% OE Replacement

If this is your trampoline, this mat is a perfect replacement for the original in thickness, stitching and quality of nylon tabs and galvanized rings. The only difference is the branding printed on the center and a vinyl cover over the stitching to protect from UV (better than the original being replaced from 2008).

You WILL need a spring tool and at least a second set of hands to install (or at least hand you springs). And the mat will seem too small at first.

TO INSTALL:
(read through all steps before starting)

NOTE 1: Counting mat rings / frame holes accurately is essential. Get off by 1 and you have to start over.

NOTE 2: Be careful to pull springs straight out (and keep an eye on it as you're pulling) from the mat ring to the frame hole so that the spring stays hooked in the point of the ring. Do not allow the spring to slip to one of the sides or a cascade of problems will ensue.

1) Select a ring on the mat and attach a spring to it and to the trampoline frame

2) Count 42 rings around on the mat and attach another spring

3) Count 42 holes around on the frame and attach the other end of that spring

4) Count 21 rings from either spring and add the next spring; do the same for holes and attach

5) Repeat step 4 on the opposite side

(You now have 4 springs attached at each of the 90º points, creating 4 quadrants)

6) In your first quadrant, count 10 rings and holes from a spring and attach another

7) In the quadrant directly across from your first, count 10 rings and holes and attach another

8) Repeat for the other 2 quadrants

9) Now start filling in the gaps, alternating to the opposite side every couple of springs. The idea is to keep alternating sides so that the tension remains as even as is possible.

***It might seem easier to just start working your way around, but the pull will become uneven, increasing the likelihood of having a ring slip.***

Feel free to message me for any further info.

title: The plight of the Third World
text:
Accomplished master of the police procedural Henning Mankell strays from this genre in his latest novel, "Kennedy's Brain". In his novel, Mankell in the guise of a mystery, has penned what is in reality a social commentary. Mankell who resides at least partially in Mozambique, takes aim at the plight of the African underprivileged particularly relating to the AIDS epidemic and it's exploitation by the pharmaceutical companies.

Swedish archaeologist Louise Cantor whose specialty is ancient Greek artifracts is leading an expedition in Greece sponsored by Uppsala university. She happily anticipates taking a break to return to Stockholm and visit her son Henrik. Much to her shock and dismay she arrives at his flat, unable to raise him on the phone, to find him lying dead in bed. She is stunned to learn that an autopsy confirms that he overdosed on barbiturates.

Unable to believe that Henrik would take his own life she commences her own investigation. She travels across the world to a remote area of Australia to recruit her estranged husband Aron and inform him of their son's death. Together they go through his papers that direct them to an apartment their son kept in Barcelona. Hacking into his computer they discover that he was HIV positive and that he had business that took him to Mozambique.

Louise Cantor proceeds to Africa after the mysterious disappearance of her ex husband. While there she is confronted by danger and the horrors of a village designed to care for AIDS victims where Henrik had worked. She discovers that there is quite a bit more going on there than administering to the sick.

Mankell paints a graphic picture of the misery endured by the suffering in Africa while being critical of those who opportunistically use them for financial gain. The plot of "Kennedy's Brain", metaphor for an inexplicable and secretive mystery is very much similar to Le Carre's "The Constant Gardener".

title: High Adrenaline Thriller with quirks
text:
Music Notes is Manning Wolfe's second installation in the Texas Lady Lawyer series. It's a fast-paced, intense thriller with an eclectic cast, one of those stories that will keep you up so late at night you'll need extra coffee in the morning. Merit Bridges, the perky but powerful protagonist and her quirky team of paralegals find themselves, yet again, in opposition to a deliciously delusional villain intent on their demise.
When the rehabilitated rock guitar hero, Liam Nolan, is brutally murdered with his own guitar, Merit is not only responsible for his estate but feels morally obligated to help solve the crime. Enter Davey Ray Bell who claims to be Liam's love child. Though Davey seems lost and alone there may be some validity to his claim. Meanwhile, Liam's former manager, L A Baron, hopes to grab all the glory and the cash. When he fails to convince the legal authorities of his claim to the riches, he uses his vast resources to attempt to destroy Merit's career and reputation.
The writing is very visual and personal. Wolfe's characters are complex and for the most part driven by more than just material gain. Though the story is definitely dark, it's handled with a quirky humor and panache that brings this storyteller to the pinnacle of legal thriller authors. As an extra bonus, it's set in Austin Texas where the old hippie culture still clashes with the techno-boom of the early 21st century. Wolfe's Texas Lady Lawyer stories scream to be made into a Showtime summer miniseries featuring Reese Witherspoon and her ponytail as the protagonist. Check your local listings, but as always read the book first.

text:
I bought this book as a gift for my father, who has spent his entire adult life working in the industrial Midwest. It was a challenging subject, as his community often feels misunderstood or overlooked by coastal media narratives, but this book handles the topic with such profound empathy and journalistic integrity that it resonated deeply with him. The author does not offer easy answers or cheap political talking points. Instead, he takes the time to truly listen to the people living in the flyover states, capturing their fears, their dignity, and their complex relationship with modern America.

The narrative structure is compelling, weaving personal anecdotes with broader economic and cultural analysis without ever feeling academic or detached. I found myself reading late into the night, genuinely moved by the human stories at the center of the argument. It is rare to find a work that challenges you to think differently without being preachy. My father actually set it down multiple times to reflect on passages, which rarely happens with non-fiction. This is not just a book about politics; it is a testament to the resilience of the American spirit. It has sparked meaningful conversations at our dinner table about topics we usually avoid. If you are looking for a nuanced, heart-wrenching, and ultimately hopeful look at what makes this country tick, this is essential reading. It deserves every star and more for its courage and clarity.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I picked this up on a whim, mostly because the description promised to cut through the noise of modern political discourse, and I am so glad I did. As someone who generally finds political theory dry and overly academic, I was surprisingly hooked from the very first chapter. The author has a rare gift for taking complex, tangled concepts and unraveling them with clarity and humor that never feels condescending. It does not feel like reading a textbook; it feels more like having a deep, insightful conversation with a wise friend who genuinely wants you to understand how the machinery of power really works.

What struck me most was the relevance. You might expect a book on politics to feel dated quickly, but the arguments here are timeless. The historical examples are chosen with precision, and the parallels to current events are drawn without being heavy-handed. I found myself pausing often to highlight passages that challenged my own assumptions, which is the sign of truly engaging non-fiction. It forced me to look at recent news cycles with a critical eye rather than just accepting the prevailing narratives. This is not just a book for politicians or academics; it is essential reading for any citizen who wants to participate more meaningfully in their democracy. It has genuinely expanded my perspective and equipped me with better tools to analyze the world around me. If you are looking for a page-turner that also enriches your mind, this is it. Five stars, easily.

Maybe it’s because I don’t agree with her portrayal of southern culture, I’m not sure. Having lived all across the southern US I find that my reality conflicts (dramatically, at times) with her portrayal of the people in these areas.

The Girl Who Stopped Swimming is the first book by Joshilyn Jackson I’ve finished, so I suppose that says a lot, but I still didn’t find it stellar. I didn’t jive with the whole ‘haunted by spirits’ thing and I found the characterization of everyone to be so cliche (the socially awkward nerd, the free-spirit sister, the disconnected teenage daughter, the white trash distant relative). text:
I bought two of these for older MBPs on 5/26/10. Within two weeks, one of them was not holding a charge and was returned for replacement without question (this speaks well of the vendor!). It's now 5 months later and the replaced battery now has a "full charge" of 4261 and a condition of "fair". This battery has a full-charge runtime of less than an hour and has been known to stop charging and shut down the computer spontaneously. All the typical Apple-recommended tricks have been tried (reset PRAM, etc) but it's the battery, not anything to do with the calibration. I cannot find a warranty statement anywhere...

The other battery has a full charge of 5032 and a condition of good. Runtime is ~2hr, and although the fit is not perfect, I'd say that this battery was worth the price.

Suspiciously enough, both batteries have identical info, including the serial number:
Model Information:
Serial Number: GSA-A1175-ASMB012-3c28-42c
Manufacturer: GSA-A1175
Device name: ASMB012
Pack Lot Code: 012d
PCB Lot Code: 050d
Firmware Version: 646e
Hardware Revision: 2800
Cell Revision: 0000

Worth the price? Not really. One out of three might be a good batting average in baseball but not for purchased products. Take your chances, you might get lucky.

title: Great value, particularly for the accessories

Fortnite's figures are great, and collecting accessories is much of the fun, but you don't usually get many accessories with basic figures--you typically either have to buy loot chests or special/deluxe sets to get accessories. The piñatas are some of the best deals due to how many accessories you get, along with a figure. Although the MSRP of a piñata is slightly higher than the price of a single figure plus a single loot chest, you get a lot more content--over twice as many accessories as what you'd get from a standard loot chest. And not all the accessories or variations can be found in other sets--so even if you already have a decent stash of accessories, some of these will probably still be new to you.

The Rust Lord figure is not the prettiest or fanciest-looking figure in the series, but he's pretty decent. A lot of the characters are very cartoony, but this guy's design is a little bit more subdued, which may or may not be a plus depending on your tastes. Like all the 4" figures, he's got a very high amount of articulation and pretty sophisticated construction, so you'll want to be a little careful with him at first. If any joints seem stuck, try soaking him in hot water briefly to loosen them up and lessen the risk of breakage. I haven't had any problems with any of my figures yet, but be aware it can happen. I wouldn't recommend these for very young kids due to their relatively complex design.

And yes, the packaging is really a sort of piñata. It's designed for you to be able to bash it open. You can probably open it up without destroying it if you are careful. Be aware that there's a lot of confetti inside, in case you do decide to break it open.

title: The Eternal Truth of the Simple Man
text:
Norwood Pratt has neither guile nor an education, but he possesses a comic wisdom that guides him from one nutty encounter to another. He is the man he is, regardless, slow to fight but ready to fight, honest, to a point, and rationalizing beyond that. He never internalizes, seldom jumps to conclusions, and just proceeds along the rightness of his course without question. He is a Faulknerian character distilled down to the basics, so unsophisticated he is hilariously honest.

Norwood is a fast-paced comedy of the simpleton winning out in the end because his sights are so low he can't lose, and Charles Portis' social commentary should not be missed, but if you do, the dialogue alone is worth the read. And if the characters in Norwood seem too silly to be real? Well, I recognized them more than I care to admit.

title: A little disappointed
text:
Michael Fallon's Dodgerland is an attempt to put the Dodger teams of 1977 and 1978 into the author's view of their cultural context.

When he writes about the way that new manager Tommy Lasorda prepared the team for the challenges of the '77 season, or the contentious Dodger clubhouse, he provides valuable insights. As a fan, these were some of my favorite Dodger teams of all time and maybe the best that I have ever seen play, even though they didn't win the World Series until 1981, so I found the "inside game" stuff interesting.

I could do with the liberal politics that the author espoused in the guise of a baseball book - as a lifelong Californian, I don't hold the author's favorable view of mayor Tom Bradley.

The author also makes the book a little autobiographical, choosing to write about his dad's hardware store and the author's role in the business. He also writes about a number of seemingly disjointed things, like skateboarding, author Tom Wolfe and other odds and ends.

He also makes some unforced errors - factual mistakes about the baseball stuff.

Overall interesting but not nearly as good as it could be.

If you consider yourself pro-Palestinian, I challenge you to read this text. If you are pro-Israeli, Christian Zionist, or Jewish Zionist, I challenge you to read this text. title: Great fragrance!  Horrible shampoo!
text:
I really wanted to love this shampoo because the scent is absolutely incredible. As soon as you open the bottle, it smells like a high-end luxury spa. It has these beautiful, sophisticated notes that linger in the air and make the actual process of washing your hair feel like a treat. If I were rating this based on fragrance alone, it would be a five-star product without question. Unfortunately, a shampoo needs to actually function as a cleanser and conditioner, and this one fails miserably in that department.

The first thing I noticed was the texture. It is far too thin, almost watery, which meant I had to use twice as much as usual just to get it to lather. Even then, the lather was weak and didn't feel like it was actually lifting any oil or buildup from my scalp. After rinsing, my hair felt strangely tacky, as if there was a film left behind that wouldn't wash away.

The real disaster happened once my hair dried. I have medium-textured hair that is usually manageable, but after using this, my strands felt like straw. It stripped every bit of moisture from my hair, leaving it frizzy, tangled, and completely lifeless. I spent twenty minutes trying to brush through the knots, and I genuinely feared I was going to cause breakage. It felt as though the chemicals used to create that amazing scent completely overwhelmed the moisturizing ingredients, or perhaps there weren't any moisturizing ingredients to begin with.

I tried using a deep conditioner afterward to save my hair, but the damage was already done. My scalp also felt itchy and tight for a few hours after the wash, which makes me suspect that the fragrance is too strong or the formula is too harsh for sensitive skin.

It is such a shame because I love the way it smells, and I almost considered using it as a body wash just to keep the scent around, but for the price point, I expect a hair product to actually improve the condition of my hair. I cannot recommend this to anyone who cares about the health of their locks. Save your money and buy a shampoo that prioritizes hair care over perfume. It is a lovely scent, but a horrible shampoo.

title: A fun political satire and much more…
text:
The First Lady Escapes is obviously a satire of the current political atmosphere, but it is also an enjoyable, well thought-out story with a fun cast of characters. As I was reading the story, I found myself falling in love with several of them, especially Angel, the gay Mexican hairdresser, and Moon, a FLOTUS impersonator, and I was eagerly anticipating what would happen as each new chapter began. The short chapters are titled with a location and time to add to the fun so the reader can feel the excitement build as events unfold simultaneously at the White House and across the US and Mexico.

While the President is the focus of the political satire, FLOTUS and the characters who become part of her journey are well-developed and bring the story to life. The detailed descriptions of their surroundings and activities made me feel like I was escaping to Mexico with FLOTUS or part of the White House luxury being experienced for the first time by FLOTUS’ impersonator.

I picked up this book because I was intrigued by the premise and hoped for a few moments of escapism from the daily news. I got that and so much more. The author acknowledges the current political situation inspired her to write this satire, but beyond that initial premise, she created an entertaining story with well developed characters that evolve to show the people behind traditional stereotypes whether they are immigrants, paparazzi, or transgender. This is definitely not a read for supporters of the current administration. But for everyone else who has felt concern, frustration, or outrage as they read the latest news feeds, this book will put a smile on your face and even let you laugh out loud and be entertained for a few fun hours.

title: This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year
text:
This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year. It was a nice surprise, being a debut novel about parenthood: it could have gone either way.

As the synopsis says, this is a character-driven story, and that’s what makes it so interesting and enjoyable. These are people that any toddler parent knows all too well. If you’ve ever been in a playgroup or online parenting forum/group, you can relate on some level to this book (albeit an extreme version of reality). It’s a look into modern parenting, in a yuppie world where everyone is following their own “parenting truth” and trying not to judge (though failing at doing so) others’. It is also a window into the complexities of “early-mid”adult life (if you can all it that)- relationships with others and with ourselves, and what is most important for each of us.

This book will make you smile, cringe and even think a little bit. What are the sacrifices we make for our families, for our loved ones, for our children? What are the personal costs? What wouldn’t we do to find some meaning behind the every day mundane? What is the difference between friendship and support?

I recommend it for any parent of young(ish) kids looking for an enjoyable summer read.

title: A Very Good Electric Shaver for Sensitive Skin
text:
As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

text:
The package comes with two jar openers. I'm still not sure what to do with the second one because my kitchen isn't all that large, so for now I guess I've got a spare. :) I was a little skeptical of the adhesive, because not only does the jar opener need to stick upside down to the bottom of the cabinet, but it also needs to resist the torque of turning the jar every time you use it. Well, so far so good. It's still adhering to my cabinet bottom and it still works.

There are these little metal teeth on one side of the v-shaped recess. You just slide the jar into the recess as far as it will go and turn. The metal teeth grip the lid, so when you turn, you're actually unscrewing the jar from the lid instead of the lid from the jar. And it's really easy. Admittedly, I don't have arthritis in my hands, so I can't say how easy it would be with arthritis. But I am a single woman with limited arm and grip strength. Jars can be a challenge. Opening them with this is safer than banging on the edge of the lid with the handle of a butter knife. And easier, too.

I'd give it 5 stars, but I can't help but wonder about the longevity of the adhesive. Maybe if it's hanging upside down under my cabinet a year from now I'll come back and give it the 5th star. And yes, I did get this item at a reduce price in order to review it, but that does not effect my review. If you don't have integrity, what have you got?

It does not just describe the current political landscape; it provides a framework for understanding why things are the way they are and how we might move forward. 

Whether you are a political science student or someone who generally avoids the news because it feels overwhelming, this book is a must-read. It provided me with a sense of clarity that I have been searching for in other texts. I highly recommend picking this up if you want to deepen your understanding of the world around you. Now I am stuck with a bottle that I have to manually unscrew and pour out, which defeats the purpose of buying a pump-action dispenser for hygiene and portion control. It feels like the manufacturer cut corners on the materials to save money, and it completely ruins the user experience. I cannot recommend this to anyone who values durability. title: 3 Stars

This is another book that left me feeling unsure of how I felt about it. It was such a good book. I didn't want to put it down! So compelling, I HAD to know what would happen next. Time after time, I would feel my jaw almost drop open. Some of the plot twists I did not expect to see coming. The ending, however, is what left me unsure. This book was so deceptive, so unsettling, just downright creepy. The story line was amazing and definitely different than what has become the norm in psychological thrillers over the past year. It is what drew me in. The hard hitting, edge of your seat writing is what kept me going. I loved how it went from 2 different point of views- Jessica and Dr. Shields. It was nice to be able to read their points of view, instead of just one characters.

I have not read The Wife Between Us, though I do own it. So I went into this book with only the hype of that book and this one. It was all anyone could talk about. If only the ending had of been different, this book would have been at least 4 stars at minimum. That ending just kind of left me hanging..........or is there going to be a sequel? I think it is definitely set up for that possibility.

title: Not consistent enough. Makes me stabby.

It seems like a great idea.
The problem is:
1. You will be constantly switching to different channels on the transmitter hoping that one of them will actually give you a clear picture that doesn’t come in and out.
2. If that’s not the problem, you will have a picture that suddenly goes black whether you’re watching live TV or any other thing from a DVR source. Additionally, if it’s not the picture AND the sound that goes out it’s just the sound while you watch characters on your TV move their mouth’s without anything coming out.
3. This has no rhyme or reason as to why and when it’s going to happen. You might have a couple days where it seems to be working great and you think you’ve actually figured it out. Then you have the entire day of ridiculous frustration as you try and change the transmitter channels pausing and stopping and rewinding shows you’re watching. Meanwhile kids frustrated that their Daniel Tiger show isn’t playing.

In conclusion, my overall opinion is that if there had been any other item I could find to substitute sending our DVR to our TV, then I would’ve gone with that. Or at least tried something else with hopes it would work better. For now the only cable line we have in our entire house is at the opposite end of our living room. I am going to continue on my frustrating search to find something that works so I don’t have to drill a hole in the outside of our wall. Maybe it’s just time to give up cable altogether.

If you need a rugged, dependable speaker that sounds good and won’t break the bank, this is a solid pick. I’d buy it again.

The clip:
-It has no spring, so I am not sure how long it will last without snapping.

-It only has 180 degrees of rotation, so you can't turn it upside down (I prefer one that has 360 degrees, but for most this is probably not an issue)

This also comes with a a lanyard attached to a plug that fits into the port. This can be used instead of/as a backup to the clip.

All in all it is a good product, and I would definitely recommend it.

It clicks into place with a solid sound that assures me it is secure. I do not have to constantly check to see if my pass is still in place.

Another feature I really appreciate is the ease of access. When I arrive at the lift, I can pull the pass out quickly without fumbling with complicated zippers or buttons. This saves time and reduces friction during peak hours. The design is sleek and low-profile. It sits flat against my body, so it does not snag on anything. I have tried wearing it under layers, and it does not add significant bulk. For anyone who values their season pass and wants to avoid the stress of losing it or damaging it, this is an essential accessory. It provides peace of mind that allows me to focus entirely on the mountain. The value for the price is excellent considering how much money the season pass itself represents. Losing that pass would be a significant financial loss and an inconvenience that this small product helps prevent. I recommend it to every skier and snowboarder I know who relies on their season pass for their winter enjoyment. It is a simple solution to a common problem, executed perfectly.

text:

It’s been three years, and most of the memories are gone, but we still find Nana in my daughter’s smile, in our garden, in books and in our hearts.

Out to Sea explains all this in such a simple and profound way. Helen Kellock’s sparse text and encompassing illustrations speak right to child’s — or adult’s — heart. title: Adequate Brush But Buyer Beware
text:
I first purchased this brush back in 2013. After just a few shaves the brush separated from the handle and I started a return. I wanted a replacement, but it was out of stock so Simply Beautiful sent me a refund instead, without requiring me to return the defective brush. I decided to attempt a repair of the brush. This time the seller, Simply Beautiful, sent me a replacement. The replacement seems to be performing fine after a few weeks of usage. So far, so good.

In summary, I like the brush. It suits my needs. But I am disappointed in the manufacturing of the product.
If you order one of these be prepared for this issue. And maybe have some Marine Epoxy on hand.

As a side note, it is not unusual for some brushes to have a "wet dog" odor when new. This can be remedied by repeatedly soaking the brush in soapy water overnight. Through normal usage the odor will eventually go away.

empty them frequently. The unit that is in our trailer is unheated and
will occasionally freeze up during the winter; it continues to run but
the vents get covered in ice so no more moisture collects in the water
tank. But we bring it into the house and, after the ice thaws, the unit
resumes normal operation. We'll continue to use this product and
replace them as needed, but now I spend the extra $1 or 2 for the
extended warranty (which I haven't had to use yet). Overall, I would
rate this product as a 4 on a scale of 1-5, 5 being the highest. The
only reason I don't give it a 5 is the high failure rate and not being
able to figure out whether the failure is in the unit itself or in the
power supply so that the entire unit doesn't need to be thrown away when

text: I am writing this review with extreme frustration and disappointment after having this bed frame literally collapse under me during the first week of ownership. It wasn't just a loose screw; the metal itself had twisted and deformed, leaving the entire mattress sagging dangerously low to the floor. I contacted customer support immediately, providing photos and my order number, but they have been ghosting me for five days now. There is no response to my emails, which is the worst part of this entire experience. Not only did I lose the product, but I also spent my Saturday trying to figure out how to move a mattress without a proper frame. I would not recommend this to anyone, not even my worst enemy. The materials feel cheap and flimsy, lacking any structural integrity. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you are looking for a bed frame, spend the extra few dollars on a reputable brand that actually stands up to normal use. This was a total failure from start to finish, and I am furious that I have to dispose of this dangerous, broken junk myself. Save your time, save your money, and avoid this product at all costs. title: Straightforward in an unspectacular way
text:
Since Mark Waid introduced a group of lab assistants to work under Bruce Banner, I’ve harped on the fact that they’ve had very little in the way of character development. The Indestructible Hulk #16 finally addresses that issue by delving into the past of Mr. Jessup, largely because, as this issue informs us, he’s going to die within a week. Spending a full issue to build up a character just so readers will feel some sort of impact when he dies seems a little cheap to me, but I still think this marks progress, as one of the things this book has been lacking is a good supporting cast.

The art here is done by Mahmud Asrar, who does a pretty good job. Nothing here really blows me away, but it’s a welcome change to have an entire issue follow one art style after the last arc cycled through multiple artists on a page-by-page basis.

As a whole, this issue does what it needs to do in a straightforward if unspectacular way. We finally get some background on some of Banner’s supporting cast, we get the suspense of knowing that said character is going to die, and we get some Hulk smashing action. This is an above-average issue that will hopefully lead into bigger things to come when the story gets rolling.

The central character, Maureen, is wonderfully drawn—fierce, flawed, and utterly human. Her journey through her journey she goes on feels authentic, and there are moments of real emotional weight. The dialogue crackles, and the author clearly has a deep understanding of the small, quiet triumphs that define a life.

That said, I found some of the subplots underdeveloped. A few side characters appear promising but then fade into the background without resolution. The ending also felt a bit rushed, as if the author was trying to wrap things up too neatly after such quickly that the emotional payoff didn’t quite land. It’s a solid read, but not the knockout I was hoping for.

If you enjoy it for the strong central character and the vivid writing, but go in knowing that not every thread gets tied off neatly. If you like character-driven stories with a slightly imperfect finish, this will still be worth your time. Four stars from me—good, but not great.
