I have been using this device for about three weeks now, and overall, I am quite happy with the purchase. When shopping for electronics in this category, I usually worry about the build quality and whether the product actually lives up to the marketing claims. In this case, it mostly does.

The setup process was straightforward, and it integrated with my existing home setup without any major hiccups. Performance-wise, it is snappy and reliable. I haven't experienced any significant lags or crashes, which is a huge relief compared to the last brand I tried. The design is sleek and fits well on my desk, and the materials feel durable enough to last for a few years of regular use.

The only reason I am giving it four stars instead of five is the battery life. While it is decent, it doesn't quite reach the advertised hours mentioned in the description. I find myself plugging it in a bit more often than I expected. Additionally, the included charging cable is surprisingly short, which limits where I can place the device while it is powering up.

That being said, these are minor grievances compared to the actual utility of the product. It does exactly what it is supposed to do, and the price point makes it a great value for the money. If you are looking for a dependable piece of gear that doesn't break the bank, this is a solid choice. I would recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable daily driver and doesn't mind a quick charge every now and then.

title: Amstaff mom approved!!!!
text:
This collar is a life saver!
We have a nearly one year old American Amstaff that is the single most stubborn hard headed dog in the entire world. After paying ungodly amounts of money on training & behavior classes, we were at wits end with our boy. Any time we let him out the door he would take off like his tail was on fire & it was nearly impossible to get him to come back until he was good and ready. This collar has made a gigantic improvement in his behavior outside. We don't even normally have to use the shock function. Most of the time the vibrate option scares him into action & works perfectly.

The packaging was great, while there were little to no instructions in the product box, or on the box, with a little trial & error we figured it out pretty quickly.
The charger seems to work amazing. As instructed I charged the unit for 6 hours after opening. We've been using the collar for about a 1-2 weeks now and it's STILL RUNNING on THAT FIRST CHARGE! Granted we only use the collar for potty & outside time. So that's probably a big factor in our extended battery life.

We haven't had any issues with the collar itself. My pupper is a very broad Amstaff so his neck girth is pretty substantial, and the collar included fit with plenty of room to spare. We also have not had any skin issues with where the prongs sit on our boy. Again, he doesn't continuously wear the collar, which is probably a contributing factor. I could see where the prongs could potentially be an issue if the use of the unit wasn't closely supervised. Leaving it on your dog for long periods of time, in the same spot, without adjusting could definitely be hazardous to a dog.

All in all, we absolute live this collar. It was extremely affordable and a great quality for the price. Honestly, I'm surprised it's not higher. Great purchase.

title: The candles themselves look and feel like REAL wax candles - because they are
text:
Wow! This is a very well thought out and fully functional product! Well done! The candles themselves look and feel like REAL wax candles - because they are! It just doesn't get any better. Some things to consider ...
1. As stated, because the candles are made from real wax, you can use "melted" wax to anchor the candles solidly in your candle holders so they remain straight and stable like you normally wood. Great!
2. These wax candles are actually "hollow cylinders" with a removable metal inner cylinder that houses the two AA batteries that power the flame apparatus at the top. This is significant because when the time comes to change the batteries as needed, you can simply pull the inner cylinder out of the wax casing from the top and then simply slide it back in the wax casing. The beauty of this comes from the fact that the wax cylinder remains firmly anchored in your candle holders so you don't have to scrap the melted wax in the cups and re-set them. Very, very convenient!
3. The included remote works terrifically! If you want to conserve battery life you must manually "push down" in the flame top (just like clicking a ball point pen) to completely shut them down and must "click them on" again for your next use.

Bottom line, the flame is not the same as having the real thing but given all of the pluses and convenience, these candles are by far the next best thing. To the makers of this product, it's time for WHITE (and more) candles! I'd buy two sets today!

text:
I'm kind of a cheapskate, so I was a little iffy on spending this much on a bird toy, especially with our parakeet cage filled with $1 plastic bird toys. Luckily, this purchase was definitely worth it! Our parakeets ignored it for a few days before cautiously approaching it, but after a week, they were going absolutely insane over it. I expected it to just be a bowling toy, but our parakeets found more ways to play with it than expected, which was a huge plus and something that we hadn't seen with a lot of the other toys, where they just chew and climb. They like chewing and pulling at the bowling pins, the chains holding the pins, the brown "railing" that the bowling ball is attached, to, and of course, the bowling ball itself. It took a little while longer for them to pull the top part of the stick on the ball to hit the pins, but they eventually did figure it out. The mirror was also a plus, since our keets LOVE mirrors. One of our parakeets likes sticking his head into the hole under the bar and moving everything with his face (he apparently likes doing this with a lot of things ;D)

The toy itself was very easy to install. The nut and screw mechanism keeps the toy securely attached to the cage. Our parakeets sometimes climb on top of the toy while playing, and it's fastened securely enough to support that. Build quality is also very good, and the toy is easy to clean.

Edit: We cleaned the cage and moved stuff around, and it looks like our parakeets didn't like the new location, as they ignored the toy for over 2 weeks. We changed the location again, and they're all over it again! So if you've had your toy in the cage for a while and your birds are used to its presence, but they're not playing with it, maybe moving it elsewhere could help!

title: Make Light Work
text:
[[VIDEOID:73bf56891aed34f39e2209128c231a2c]] The Crookes Radiometer, or "Light-Mill," is a fascinating scientific conversation piece that seems to convert light directly into motion. My DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is a superb example of the simple device that confused even its eminent discoverer. I generally keep my radiometer on my desk, where it has started many good conversations. Radiometers are actually driven by infrared light; a small reptile cage heater tucked behind the books on one side of my desk makes it spin like a top, and turning the heater on and off has given me some fun with visitors to my office.

This DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is fragile and should be kept away from little hands - being made of glass with a partial vacuum inside it's as breakable as an old-fashioned light bulb. But as a scientific display and conversation piece it's tough to beat this seemingly simple but elegantly made toy. I'm delighted with my DORAMI Radiometer and recommend it highly.

title: Just one question:  Why?
text:
In five editions (and counting of the Physical Basis for the Direction of Time) Dieter Zee has been asking the same question: What laws of the universe are actually law like and what laws of the universe are merely fact like?

This is a question very much at the heart of this brief accessible tome wherein Great Britain's Royal Astronomer probes the significance of two microscopic numbers and four macroscopic numbers that seem to effect the raison d'etre of the universe.

Along the way we deal with claims such as the cosmic anthropologic hypothesis which assert that the universe was created specifically the way it was in order to allow life (an assertion a little like Goldfish saying that the aquarium in which they live and the country house that supports it was created specifically for them).

Things happen and unless you're Paul Davies and writing any of his major works on the matter (starting with God and the New Physics proceeding to the award winning Mind of God and finally concluding with the hard back title Cosmic Jackpot) we are merely "a thing that happened."

Humbling no doubt but a likely consequence of fraction of a fraction of fraction of...you get the point...of our occupying the merest miniscule part of creation.

But this book is important reading. Like any good reporting it lays out the conventional wisdom (of 1999, still sadly all too current in 2009) and leaves the reader to decide.

Why? In it's ultimate sense the question will always remain a personal one. But at least science can say, and purport to actually prove, that we're in there somewhere.

Additionally, while it is dishwasher safe, I found that food particles tend to get stuck in the small crevices near the rim, making it a bit tedious to clean thoroughly by hand. For the price point, I expected a bit more ergonomic design for brachycephalic breeds. It does the job, but it is not the revolutionary solution I anticipated. It is a decent intermediate option, but if your pet is very resistant to change, you might want to consider alternatives that are less drastic in shape. Overall, it is a functional product that serves its basic purpose, even if it lacks some user-friendly features that would make it a five-star item.

title: Where's the apricot?
text:
I finally decided to treat myself to a proper facial moisturizer after years of neglecting my skin barrier due to stress and harsh weather conditions. The packaging of Where's the apricot? is quite striking, with its minimalist white bottle and simple typography that immediately suggests a clean, clinical approach to skincare. This aesthetic alone was enough to make me confident that I was making a sensible investment in my daily routine. The product arrived quickly and was well-protected, which is always a relief when ordering fragile glass containers online.

Upon opening the bottle, the first thing I noticed was the scent. It has a very distinct, fresh aroma that reminds me slightly of citrus but with a subtle nutty undertone, likely from the apricot kernel oil mentioned on the label. It is not overpowering or perfumed in a way that feels artificial. Instead, it smells natural and inviting, which sets a pleasant tone for my morning skincare ritual. I have combination skin, which means I usually struggle to find a moisturizer that hydrates without making my T-zone look greasy by midday. This product has managed to strike a surprising balance.

I have been using it consistently for about three weeks now. The texture is lightweight and absorbs into the skin relatively quickly, leaving behind a soft, supple finish rather than a heavy, occlusive layer. I noticed a significant improvement in the dryness around my nose and cheeks, areas that usually flare up during colder months. My skin feels more resilient and less reactive to environmental changes. However, I am giving this product four stars instead of five for one specific reason. While the hydration is excellent, I found that for my oily zones, I might need to use a slightly lighter layer or perhaps pair it with a mattifying powder during the day to maintain shine control. It works well, but it requires a bit of adjustment depending on where you apply it on your face.

The ingredients list is transparent and reassuring, focusing on natural oils and gentle botanicals. I appreciate that there are no harsh sulfates or artificial fragrances cluttering the formula. For anyone looking for a straightforward, effective moisturizer that does exactly what it promises without unnecessary gimmicks, this is a strong contender. It is not a miracle worker that will erase years of sun damage overnight, but it is a reliable staple for maintaining healthy, hydrated skin. The price point is reasonable for the quality of the formula, and I expect to repurchase this once I finish the current bottle. It has earned its place on my bathroom shelf as a consistent, trustworthy part of my regimen.

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this wheel to replace a worn-out one on my son's stunt scooter, and overall, I am quite happy with the purchase. When you are looking for a larger wheel, the main goal is usually to get a smoother ride over rougher pavement and a bit more stability at higher speeds. This product definitely delivers on that front.

The build quality is impressive. The core feels sturdy and doesn't seem like it will crack under pressure during jumps or hard landings. The polyurethane material is dense and has a good grip on the road, which gives a lot more confidence when carving or turning sharply. Compared to the smaller stock wheels that came with the scooter, these make a noticeable difference in how the ride feels. The vibration from the asphalt is significantly reduced, and it takes a bit more effort to maintain speed, but it glides much further once you get going.

The installation process was straightforward, although I did have to double-check my bearings. The wheel fits perfectly on the axle without any wobbling. I noticed that the color is slightly different from the images online, but it is still a nice, vibrant shade that looks great on the deck.

The reason I am giving this four stars instead of five is that I noticed a tiny bit of flat-spotting after about two weeks of heavy use. My son tends to skid and brake hard, and while the wheels are durable, they aren't completely immune to wear and tear. I think they are great for general riding and moderate stunts, but if you are a professional-level rider doing extreme grinds every single day, you might find them wearing down faster than the premium high-end brands. However, for the price point, the value is exceptional.

If you are looking to upgrade a basic scooter to make it feel more "premium" and smooth, this is a fantastic choice. It transforms the ride from a bumpy, jittery experience into something much more fluid. I would definitely recommend these to any parent or rider who wants a larger wheel without spending a fortune. Just be mindful of how hard you brake if you want them to last as long as possible. It is a solid, reliable piece of equipment that does exactly what it claims to do.

title: Great Nutcracker
text:
I’ve been through more nutcrackers than I care packers than I care to count—flimsy metal ones that bend, wooden ones that splinter, and those cheap lever-style models that barely crack a walnut without crushing the meat flying everywhere. I finally decided to try the Great Nutc the Great Nutcracker, and honestly, it lives up to the name. 

The first thing I noticed is the build quality. It’s made of heavy-duty cast metal with a solid, comfortable grip. No wobble, no flex—just a clean, decisive crack every time. I tested it on pecans, almonds, walnuts, and even a few stubborn hazelnuts. The hinge mechanism is smooth and the cracking chamber is well-designed; it holds the nut securely so you don’t have to chase pieces around the counter. Shells split cleanly, and the meat comes out in large, intact pieces far more often than with my old tools.

Cleaning is easy? The smooth surfaces wipe down quickly, and it doesn’t rust or discolor. I’ve had mine for three months of heavy holiday use and it still looks and works like new. The only minor note is that very small nuts like pistachios aren’t ideal—but that’s true of any standard cracker. For everything else, this is the best nutcracker I’ve owned. If you do a lot of baking or just enjoy fresh nuts, this is a worthwhile investment. Highly recommended.

title: MacBook Air M1: Cracking on corners after a few months.
text: I was genuinely excited to upgrade to the new MacBook Air M1, anticipating the promise of a lightweight, powerful, and durable machine for my daily workflow. Unfortunately, my experience has been nothing short of disappointing, particularly regarding the build quality. After only three months of careful, normal use, I noticed small but noticeable cracks appearing on both bottom corners of the chassis. This is not a result of any drops or impacts; the laptop sat securely in my bag, which is lined with protective padding, yet the aluminum casing simply gave way under minimal stress. It seems the structural integrity of the bottom case is severely compromised, making this device far less robust than its predecessor or even other laptops in this price range. For a product that costs over a thousand dollars, I expected a level of durability that withstands everyday commuting and handling without falling apart. I have since contacted Apple Support, but the repair process is tedious and the incident feels like a design flaw rather than a random manufacturing defect. It is frustrating to invest in premium hardware only to watch it deteriorate so quickly. I cannot recommend this model to anyone who values longevity or build quality. If you are looking for a reliable machine that won’t show signs of wear and tear in just a few months, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere. The performance is fine, but the physical durability is unacceptable for the price point.

title: Digital Babylon and Faithful Christians
text:
We live in a digital world, and one in which it seems Christians are swimming against the tide. Those who are coming to Christ in their youth within the digital age are often finding themselves lost in the sea. While following Jesus hasn't changed since Paul, it does look different from generation to generation. In an age of instant connection, limitless information, and constant entertainment, all filled with a value system that opposes God, "Faith for Exiles" asks the question of how we can create lasting disciples within this digital Babylon. In the digital age, "the goal of discipleship is to develop Jesus followers who are resiliently faithful in the face of cultural coercion and who live a vibrant life in the Spirit." David Kinnaman, president of @barnagroup, and @mattmatlock present 5 practices for Christians in the digital age.
•
1. Intimacy with Jesus to form resilient identity. Does Jesus bring you joy? Is worship a lifestyle? Is Scripture relevant to your life? Is your relationship with Jesus personal and intimate?
2. Develop muscles of cultural discernment. Is the Bible teaching at your church relevant to your life? Do you receive wisdom on how to live in a secular age? Is your worldview Christian?
3. Form meaningful, intergenerational friendships. Do you feel like you belong at church? IS someone encouraging you spiritually? Do you have personal close friends at church?
4.Train for vocational discipleship. Do you use your unique talents to honor God? Do you recognize God's unique calling on your life? Do you serve others in your church?
5. Engage in countercultural mission. Do you desire for others to see Jesus reflected in your life? Do you feel a responsibility to tell others about Jesus? Does the mission of the Church excite you?
•
This book seeks to create resilient individuals who cling to the truths of who they are in Christ, their purpose on earth, and the ways we serve and evangelize others. This book is packed front to back with research, statistics, diagrams, and charts. But the true fruit of the book comes in the theological insight and assessment of the next gen. The entire book is also gorgeously designed thanks to @chazrusso. **book graciously provided by Baker Books for an honest review

Shopping list for this TV+this stand:
(4) M6x40mm bolts

title: Cute Counting Book With Wonderful Illustrations
text: The best thing about "10 Turkeys in the Road" is indeed the turkeys, along with the rest of the illustrated material.  The artwork is superb - colorful, whimsical, and downright funny.  In this counting primer, a farmer's path becomes blocked by 10 turkeys.  The frustrated farmer tries everything to move the turkeys out of his way, but can manage to clear only one turkey at a time from his path.  Preschooler's will undoubtedly love the winsome pictures, and engaging them in the turkey counting shouldn't be difficult.  If there is any criticism to be made, however, it would be the slightly less engaging poetic narrative.  Another well-known counting book, "Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed," offers a significantly more memorable poetic experience by way of it's almost sing-song verse: "Five little monkeys jumping on the bed, one fell off and bumped his head; mama called the doctor and the doctor said, 'No more monkeys jumping on the bed!'"  I've read that one with both of my kids over the years, and the catchy rhythm & rhyme of its language make it a classic.  This book doesn't quite match that one with it's poetry, but the superb illustrations make it worthwhile.  A fine choice for little ones working on their counting skills.

Studies have linked PFAS chemicals to testicular, kidney, liver and pancreatic cancer; weakened childhood immunity, low birth weight, endocrine disruption, increased cholesterol, and weight gain in children and dieting adults.

The main point of the book is that much of the modern day conservative movement can trace it roots back to the resistance to integration in the late 50's, 60's and 70's  and that Atlanta and its metro area is the perfect example of this shift that occurred nation wide.  What makes this book so good is that it does not assume anything and traces the events in very meticulous detail describing the constantly shifting alliances in the black/white coalition in Atlanta and the though processes on both sides of the issues and while I personally found it very difficult to be sympathetic to those wanting to maintain the status quo,  after reading this book I could see how they got to the ideological point that they re now.  This book is a must read for anyone interested  in the History of political movements in American and the south especially!

text:
With her ususal excellent style and story telling skills, Ruth Rendell introduces us to a petty criminal and the effect he has on several of his victoms--lonely, vulnerable women. Somewhere in the middle of the novel, by an unfortunate (or fortunate) coincidence he meets his death in a moveie theater by the hand of a former victim. The second part is dedicated to the effect this deathhas on his victims. As usual in Rendell's novels, we are exposed to her much praised talent to draw in fine psycological detail her charcaters. Because of that, Rendell's novels carry some form of social significance that take them beyond the mystery level. And as usual, this book is a page turner.
However, in this particular novel, she has too many characters and, respectively, too many social issues/implications going on that do not always come together as planned. We have a gay MP that is relevied when he is forced to come out (social responsibiltry vs. personal freedom), his wife who is not necessarily a bad mother to her kids, but still really dumb (feminist ideas vs. traditional upbringing dilemmas); a couple with opposite eating disorders that somehow get cured abd their relationship with their friend who unvoluntarily implcates them in a crime (friednship and betrayal); and all of the above are not related too much to the mystery. I just felt that she has tried to put everything into a single book leaving a lot of the questions she raises unresolved...

I have had this unit in place for a while now. Overall it is stylish however has a number of problems.

1 - Ports only accessible in the front -- if you want to rotate this unit, there is a USB-C Flat rigid cable that will stick straight out and then you need to buy a short USB-C extension cord. I personally don't want a bunch of devices in front while I am working and thought about rotating it 90 degrees. So it's doable but not without some effort.

2 - SD Card Port is Useless, Micro-SD card is stiff. I am starting to thing that my particular unit was not inspected leaving the factory. The SD card slots are incredibly tight and the larger SD card slot requires forcing the card in and then it doesn't work.

So there are a number of design flaws I have found with this unit. Personally, you are better off getting a dongle with a longer cord and just using that. Don't spend the $80 bucks to realize you got a somewhat useless unit.

If you're like me, you consider paying a little extra for the colored, pocketed ones that have slits to put thumb tags on them. That way you can organize your stuff according to title/color, for instance, all my banking papers and statements are filed under the yellow folders tagged "banking" and all the insurance papers are in red folders tagged "car insurance, health insurance," etc., and so on. Color coding makes things easier to identify, always, as opposed to seeing those bland green or manila folders in the drawer and you've got to thumb through them for awhile before you find the folder you're looking for. And there's so much room in these folders to condense your bills, papers, and things, that with my cell phone bills, I can nearly hold up to 4 years worth, and counting, within one folder!!! The folders are pretty sturdy with their metal sliding holders and can withstand the weight and/or the wear-n-tear of you pulling them out of the drawer and filling them every month or so. Also, the accordian-like stretchiness on the sides make them easy to condense or fill. My folders have been holding up for at least 2 years now and I'm sure they'll last me a life-time. I prefer getting these and filling up my metal filing cabinets with them as opposed to getting those plastic, flimsy filers that stand alone or come in plastic totes. title: Riddle of the Book
text:
It might seem surprising, but professional bibliographers (and I am one) invariably judge a book first by its publisher. In the case of this book, it is published by Springer, a prestigious European information conglomerate. This is important because the author of this book has notably airy qualifications as a "reporter." Digital Publishing allows everyone to be an author and anyone to be a publisher, and if you can tweet you can be a "reporter." Thus, it is truly important for readers to have some sort of crap detector in place. Unfortunately, the publisher test failed on this book.

This book has virtually no redeeming substance; Wikipedia says it better -- and cheaper. The author's writing style relies on a snotty-know-it-all approach, that is particularly irritating because he has no credentials. (As an example, he even manages to insult little Corvallis, Oregon as "a jerkwater town," even though the place is a pleasantly progressive college town). Essentially, the book is about grinding axes with political correctness uber alles.

Technically, the Kindle version of the book has way too many formatting errors and unpleasant (and unnecessary) decorative images. Why ebook publishers -- and especially wealthy publishers like Springer -- can't seem to at least look at their digital product in Kindle Previewer is a bigger riddle than Kennewick Man.

My take-away from this book is that I will no longer give Springer-Verlag an automatic pass. It's easier to lose respect than to earn it, mein Herren.

For the price, this set does everything a parent wants: it keeps the kid entertained, encourages a minimal amount of adult intervention, and it doesn’t fall apart after one session. It’s a house. It’s not the premium brand with magnetic precision engineering, but for a day-in, day-out toy that a child will actually play with instead of tossing aside after ten minutes, this fits the bill perfectly. I would buy it again for another kid, and I might even pick up a second set for my own son when he’s a little older. title: A pleasant read, but could have been much better - 3.5 stars
text:
Meet the Essex sisters: four Scottish ladies recently orphaned and left impoverished with no prospective husbands. Now wards of the perpetually inebriated Duke of Holbrook, their first mission is to marry off their eldest, the witty and sensible Teresa, or Tess, as she prefers to be called.

Growing up without the proper training that other ladies of their kind receive, Tess knows that she must marry in order to support her sisters. But what she didn't expect is that she will immediately catch the eyes of two very eligible English gentlemen. There is the Earl of Mayne, who seems to genuinely like her and whom she will most likely develop a nice, though not passionate, affection for; and then there is the very rich, though just a mere Mister, Lucius Felton, who unnerves her and whose very nearness makes her heart somersault. While Tess knows that either man is a good choice, she is torn when both men ask for her hand in marriage.

While the story started off with a great promise, the focus on establishing the characters of the four sisters overshadows what could have been a really delightful romance between Tess and Lucius. Just when you think we'd finally get some action going between the main characters, the heroine would be involved in her sisters' dramas and so the focus is once again taken away from the romance. However, the interactions between Tess and Lucius when we finally get to the part are rather sweet, and at times, funny. The little banter we get to see between them surely adds to the delight of the story.

Overall, MUCH ADO ABOUT YOU is a pleasant read and holds promise for the stories of the other Essex sisters. Next are KISS ME, ANNABEL (Annabel's story) and THE TAMING OF THE DUKE (featuring Imogen).

title: Don't buy this item
text:
I really wanted to like this, but after spending an afternoon trying to make it work, I have to warn everyone: do not waste your money. The box art looked fantastic, and the description promised hours of creative play for my seven-year-old. In reality, the product is a complete mess.

First, the pieces are cut from the thinnest, cheapest cardboard I have ever seen. They started peeling and bending the moment we tried to punch them out. Several of the interlocking tabs snapped off before we even assembled the first section. The instructions are printed on a single sheet of paper in tiny, blurry font with no clear step numbering. My child and I ended up guessing how things fit together, and every guess was wrong. The final model looks nothing like the picture on the box—it wobbles, leans to one side, and falls apart if you breathe on it.

The advertised "premium sticker sheet" is actually a single sheet of low-tack stickers that refuse to stick to the textured surface. They curl up at the edges within minutes. Worse, the paint used on some of the pieces rubs off on your fingers, leaving a greasy, smudged mess. I tried contacting the seller about a missing part—the little flag that holds the main structure together was simply not in the bag. Their response was a form letter telling me to "double check" and offering a 10% refund, as if my time meant nothing.

I have bought dozens of toys and games on Amazon, and this is the first one that genuinely feels like a scam. It is not just disappointing; it is unsafe for younger kids because of the sharp plastic burrs left on the edges of some pieces that we had to file down ourselves. Save your money and buy a proper puzzle or building set from a brand that cares about quality. This thing is now in the trash, and I regret every penny I spent. I strongly advise you to avoid this product entirely.

title: Diplomacy, work, humor, and adventure in this fine memoir
text:
This is Richard Williams' fascinating and wryly humorous account of two years as the U.S. Consul General in the Chinese city of Guangzhou (formerly called "Canton") from 1979 to 1981. His was the first American consulate to re-open in China after formal diplomatic relations with the PRC were established in 1979.

Readers interested in the development of U.S.-China relations will be fascinated -- and entertained -- by this book. Large strategic and foreign policy considerations moved China and the United States to establish relations. It was left to Foreign Service Officers such as Richard Williams and his team to make it all work -- first by setting up a new Foreign Service post, then by issuing visas, establishing commercial relations, traveling through China to report on local conditions, introducing the Big Mac, and escorting the first waves of American visitors.

Americans who know the more open China of the twenty-first century will, in this book, encounter the China making its first hesitant steps toward modernization and reform. The difficulties confronted by early official travelers, the lingering suspicion of America, the obfuscation of officials high and low, and the choices made by Foreign Service families before there were international schools are all described. Williams' wife Jane had left Tianjin as a girl; her reunions with family members in the PRC add poignant touches to the book.

This is a fine book for any young person thinking about a Foreign Service career. Although almost three decades have passed since Richard Williams and his family opened the post in Guangzhou, "At the Dawn of the New China" captures much of the enduring qualities of Foreign Service life.

title: Too many subplots.
text:
There are at least half-a-dozen subplots in this book, any of which could have (and should have) been a book unto itself. As it is, Pandora's Star is a disjointed narrative, flipping from one plot to another; not randomly, but annoyingly. At least two of the subplots are tedious enough that I ultimately just started skimming over those sections or skipping them entirely. Yeah, the author had a big story he wanted to tell, and it is an interesting story, but he didn't pull it off. Oh, and to end the book so bluntly just to make us have to buy his next one is just crass commercialism on his part.

That's not to say that there aren't great elements in this massive story. But they are few and too far between to ultimately provide a satisfying experience. My advice, regrettably, is not to buy this book. And even if you can borrow it for free, don't bother reading it. There are far better "space opera" authors out there.

title: Great sprinkler for little kids!
text:
I bought this sprinkler for my three-year-old and five-year-old, and it has been an absolute lifesaver during this heatwave. We have tried a few different water toys over the last couple of summers, but most of them are either too aggressive with the water pressure or too complicated to set up. This one is perfect for little kids who are still getting used to the feeling of water spraying on them.

The setup was incredibly simple. I just hooked it up to our standard garden hose, turned on the water, and it was ready to go in less than two minutes. One thing I really appreciate is that the water pressure is gentle. My youngest can run right through the middle of it without getting overwhelmed or scared, which was a big concern for us with our previous sprinkler. It creates a fun, misty environment that keeps them cool without soaking them so instantly that they freeze up.

The build quality is surprisingly durable. My kids are not exactly gentle with their toys, and they have spent hours jumping and sliding around it, but it has held up perfectly. The material feels thick and sturdy, and we haven't noticed any leaks at the hose connection, which is usually where these things fail. It is also very easy to deflate and store away when we aren't using it, so it doesn't take up much room in the garage.

What I love most is how much active play it encourages. Instead of just sitting in a plastic pool, my kids are running, jumping, and chasing each other through the water. It keeps them physically active and completely entertained for long stretches of time. It is rare to find a toy that both children are equally obsessed with, but this has become the highlight of their day.

If you have toddlers or young children and you are looking for a way to keep them cool in the backyard without any stress, I highly recommend this. It is affordable, safe, and provides hours of entertainment. It is exactly what we were looking for to make our summer more enjoyable. I am very happy with this purchase.

I play Overwatch, CS:GO, Path of Exile, Rust, Diablo 3: RoS, GTA V, and a few others. Load times are definitely quicker with an SSD compared to a traditional HDD. I don't do heavy data transfers, so I don't reach the true potential of this drive, but I wanted to invest in the longevity and dependability with Samsung. Just be careful when looking at M.2 SSD's. NVMe's aren't compatible with certain (older) motherboards. I made that mistake when I went to buy another 970 EVO for my laptop (HP Pavilion 15). title: Loved it!  Exciting, Danger, and Loads of Adventure.
text:
Katelin has found some peace and finds she looks forward to returning and spending the summer with her grandmother. Alone, without Simon, Katelin not only finds her own adventure but encounters a young man who sends flutters through her stomach. Through the journey, Katelin and her elfin friends discover how deeply her loyalty, fearlessness and determination runs. Together they must overcome the tyrant of the Elfin world and keep the Orb out of his grasp. The only question is, is Katelin strong enough or will she bite off more than she can handle?

What a fantastic fantasy! I enjoyed the first book but was blown away by the second. Sharon Dwyer set the "worlds" up very well, the characters were very well developed; Katelin was perfect! Dwyer captured Katelin’s "attitude" and emotional well-being accurately. Dwyer skillfully wrote the stories so that her readers do/will connect with Katelin in one way or another. The connection between the worlds was realistically done - meaning the characters had believable crossover and purpose. The first book was excellent!

The second book, I LOVED! I enjoy reading books where the female character is strong without knowing it. Piney, while not a cute character in real life, became adorable and perfect for Katelin. Dwyer expertly built up the suspense between the two books and the characters. I am intrigued on how Nana and the other worlds play out in Katelin's birthright ... I suspect a twist somewhere!

Dwyer’s The Fastasmagorical Forest series is exciting, inviting and mesmerizing. Once you get into the books, there is no stepping away. Lots of fun, plot twists, and adventure.

Very well done! While a book for young adults, those of us who enjoy fantasy, magic and adventure will love this book as well! I cannot wait for the series to continue!!!

title: Incredible life — even to a layman like me
text:
First let me preface this review by saying that you should NOT be turned off to this book if you know nothing about physics or mathematics. The author does an incredible job at explaining the semantics of Diracs theories while only seldom mentioning any syntax (his explanation of the delta function was impressive).

Now on to a life worth remembering. This book does an incredible job at commemorating not only the achievements of Dirac (along with his contemporaries, always making sure credit goes where credit is due) but also the person that was Dirac. You know it’s a good book when an author makes you feel as if you knew the bloke, even though he died before I was even born and lived across the globe.
The author meticulously builds up the image and story of Dirac, with no page going to waste. I know — a book about one of the most abstract theoretical physicists to ever live, how could this be fun? Read it and prepare to be surprised!

This book not only helped fill my knowledge gaps within the history of mathematics, but also provided days of thorough entertainment.

I would recommend this book to anyone interested in the history of mathematics and one of the pioneers of Quantum Mechanics.

10/10

title: Great Little Toy for Older Children and Adults
text:
I have been a fan of toy steam engines since I received a German made WILESCO engine for Christmas in 1961! This little engine by SunnyTech, a Chinese company, is very well made, with all brass parts, except for an O-ring to seal the boiler. When I first fired the engine up it ran like who-shot-john! I was rather amazed. This will make a great gift for any budding engineers that you may know, or any professional engineers, for that matter.
There are some pitfalls that the buyer should be aware of:
There are no instructions, at least in the one I bought has no instructions, just an exploded drawing showing how it should be put together. It is a good thing that I had experience with toy steam engines.
NEVER fill the boiler more than 2/3 full.
When running, it will spray some water, this is normal for a steam engine.
It does vibrate when running, place it on a stable surface.
The engine gets HOT when running. Take appropriate precautions.
Use alcohol as a fuel. Ethel or methyl alcohol (+95%) will work best. I tried 91% Isopropyl alcohol and it works fine, although it covered the boiler with soot. So you might want to avoid that.
NEVER use any petroleum derived fuel such as gasoline or Coleman fuel.
The engine is designed to only run for a few minutes on one boiler of water. Blow the lamp out immediately when the boiler is low on water or you may damage the engine with excess heat.
Remember, this is a toy but only for older children and adults.

It also doesn’t have any strong scent or flavor, which I appreciate because I don’t want to taste my moisturizer. The tube is small but lasts a surprisingly long time with regular use. If you’re on the fence because of the humble name, don’t be. This is one of those rare products that undersells and overdelivers. text:
I picked up this book expecting stories about the most notorious rock stars, and it definitely delivers on that front. The author covers a wide range of artists from different eras, offering juicy anecdotes about their wild antics on tour and off stage. Some chapters are better than others, in my view, with the sections on the 70s and 80s being particularly engaging and well-researched. The writing style is casual and easy to read, perfect for a light read by the pool or on a commute.

But there are a few drawbacks. The book sometimes feels more like a list of scandalous events rather than a deep analysis of why these musicians behaved the way they did. I was hoping for more insight into their creative process or personal struggles, not just the party stories and hotel trashing. Also, a few of the "bad boys" profiled seemed a bit tame compared to others, making the title feel slightly exaggerated. The editing could have been tighter, as I noticed a couple of repetitive phrases slipped through.

Overall, it.

Overall, it is an entertaining read for fans of rock history and pop culture trivia, but expect surface-level treatment rather than a deep dive. Worth picking up if you want some fun behind-the-scenes tales without too much heavy analysis. Four stars.

title: Thin
text:
I wish I could give this product zero stars because it genuinely disappointed me on multiple levels. I bought the "Thin" line of dietary supplements with high hopes, expecting a subtle, perhaps unnoticeable shift in my lifestyle that would lead to results. Instead, I found myself dealing with a product that felt more like a placebo with a premium price tag attached to it. From the moment I opened the bottle, the quality was questionable. The capsules had a strange, overly powdery texture that suggested poor manufacturing standards, which immediately put me on edge regarding the actual ingredients inside.

The marketing claims were aggressive, promising noticeable thinning of fat layers within weeks without rigorous exercise or dietary changes. Let me be clear: there was nothing noticeable. I followed the instructions precisely, taking the recommended dosage every single day for four weeks. During this time, I also monitored my caloric intake and maintained my usual activity levels, so any change should have been detectable. There was none. In fact, I felt slightly more bloated in the mornings, which was the opposite of the intended effect.

Customer service was equally frustrating. When I reached out to ask if this was normal, I received a generic, automated response that offered no real solution or explanation. It felt like they were just trying to silence a complaint rather than address a potential issue with the batch. I checked online forums and found several other users reporting the same lack of efficacy, which confirms that this isn’t just bad luck on my part.

The cost is another major factor. For the price of one bottle, I could have purchased a gym membership for two months or hired a nutritionist for a consultation. Those resources would have likely yielded better, healthier, and more sustainable results than this overhyped supplement. It is clear that the brand is spending more on advertising than on effective formulation. I do not recommend this to anyone looking for genuine health improvements. Save your money and invest in whole foods and physical activity instead. This product is a waste of cash and time, and I will not be repurchasing it under any circumstances.

I would not say that this is the best book in the series, but I awaited it eagerly and finished it in one sitting without being bored.

It's a good read and possibly trite and predictable (you know the good guys are going to win, but, well, duh. As if you thought that Sauron was going to get the Ring back too).

As for the aliens, I'm gonna have to disagree that they are setting up another series, there is something in this one that seems to explain why the aliens are doing what they are doing. There have been hints in other books (book 3 had a bunch) that make them look not necessarily like bad guys. But that's just my opinion.

I hope Campbell does more books, but I just don't see him setting up another series with a war against the aliens.

title: Erik Larson leaves us wanting more...
text:
I read Erik Larson's book with great curiosity and high expectations, given the stellar reviews it has received in the media and academia. After finishing it, I have to admit I was torn between contradictory feelings:
- on one hand, the research is exhaustive and the reconstruction of the time he covers (basically July 1933-June 1934) is awesome, with great character depiction and an amazing ability to make intrigues in the State Department and events in Berlin come alive.
- on the other hand, the book left me deeply frustrated for at least 2 major reasons:

1) some major questions are left completely unanswered, esp. was Martha Dodd a Soviet spy? How did her obvious promiscuity not constitute more of an issue for the State Department, her father or a vulnerability to the German secret services?

2) even more importantly, what happens after the Night of the Long Knives (June 30, 1934)??? Dodd stayed in post until December 1937, i.e. another three and a half years (!) but barely a word is said about events during that time and his role in the American reaction to these events.

I would understand this silence if nothing had happened between June 1934 and the Anschluss, but there were extraordinary events that deserved at least a mention:
- the assassination of the Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, which led to major tension between Germany and Italy, and took place less than a month after the June 1934 "epilogue" to the book
- the Saar referendum in January 1935
- the introduction of the Nuremberg laws in September 1935
- the referendum and remilitarization of Rhineland in March 1936
- the start of the Spanish Civil war in July 1936
All of these events were major milestones in the accession of Hitler to absolute power and the unstoppable march towards a world war, and it is unthinkable that Dodd (or Larson for that matter) has nothing to say about them... If the sources or archival materials dried up after Dodd's first year in Germany, why doesn't Larson tell us so and explain why he covers only the first 22% or so of his tenure as US ambassador !!!

Overall, a great read, but one that barely scratches the surface of a fascinating subject.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I decided to upgrade my home office setup and make the switch to this professional-grade desk organizer after using a cheap plastic tray for years. On paper, this product does everything it claims to do. The build quality is certainly an improvement over the budget options, and the aesthetic fits perfectly with my modern office decor. When it first arrived, I was impressed by the weight of the materials and how sturdy it felt on my mahogany desk.

However, the actual user experience has been a bit of a mixed bag. While the overall construction is solid, the attention to detail in the design is lacking. For a product at this price point, I expected the compartments to be more intuitive. I found that while the large slots are great for notebooks, the smaller pen holders are oddly shallow. If you use a standard fountain pen or a longer gel pen, they tend to lean at an angle or slide out entirely if the desk is bumped.

The biggest issue for me is the non-slip grip on the bottom. The product description mentions high-quality rubber feet, but in reality, they are small adhesive pads that started peeling off after only two weeks of use. Now, the metal base occasionally scratches my desk surface when I slide it to reach my keyboard. I have to be incredibly careful moving it, which defeats the purpose of having an efficient workspace.

Assembly was straightforward, though the instructions were printed in a font so small I needed a magnifying glass to read them. It took about ten minutes to put together, but one of the screws didn't thread properly, leaving a slight wobble in the main shelf.

In summary, it is a decent product that looks great from a distance, but it fails on the small, practical details that actually matter during a ten-hour workday. If you are prioritizing looks over absolute functionality, you will probably be happy with this purchase. But if you are looking for a precision-engineered tool to optimize your workflow, you might want to keep looking. It is a step up from the basics, but it doesn't quite reach the level of quality I expected for the cost. It gets the job done, but it isn't perfect.

I was initially hesitant because the market is flooded with options that either sound like a rainstorm or feel like typing on solid rock. The keycaps have a nice texture that provides excellent grip without being abrasive, and the lettering is crisp and clear. But the real standout feature is the typing experience itself. The switches offer a satisfying tactile bump that confirms each keystroke without the loud clicking noise that tends to annoy my family members who work in the same room. It is quiet enough to be considerate but responsive enough to keep my typing speed at peak efficiency.

Beyond the hardware, I feel compelled to highlight the exceptional customer service I experienced. A week after receiving my order, I noticed one of the macro keys was not registering consistently. I reached out to the support team, expecting a lengthy email exchange or a demand to send the entire unit back for testing. Instead, I received a personal response within hours. The support agent was knowledgeable, polite, and proactive. They walked me through a simple troubleshooting step that instantly resolved the issue. When I mentioned that I still felt uncomfortable not having a perfect unit, they sincerely apologized for the inconvenience and processed a replacement keycap module immediately, without any hassle or hidden fees. This level of dedication to customer satisfaction is rare in the electronics industry today.

For anyone on the fence about purchasing this keyboard, I urge you to take the leap. You are not just buying a peripheral; you are investing in a tool that will enhance your daily workflow and a company that truly values its customers. The combination of premium build quality, thoughtful design, and outstanding after-sales support makes this product an absolute winner in my book. It has exceeded my expectations in every possible way, and I cannot imagine going back to a membrane keyboard. If you are looking for reliability, comfort, and a brand that stands behind its products, this is the one to get.

Perhaps I'm spoiled by churning through Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey/Maturin series and C.S. Forester's Hornblower series over the last three years, but I really had a hard time with this first Bolitho book. The writing was choppy, the characters didn't feel real, the plotting was unbelievable, and it all felt oriented towards children. Young teens, perhaps. It felt like the Hardy Boys.

The O'Brian books are fine literature - not particularly accessible, but extremely rewarding. The Forester books nail down the action/adventure genre - not as dense as O'Brian, but well-written, compelling, and fast-moving. This Bolitho book seemed to aspire to that same action/adventure niche but came up dramatically short. I'm not exactly a purist - unpretentious action/adventure books from the 1940s-1970s are a favorite of mine. But it just wasn't good.

Two stars because I didn't stop reading, I'm probably just spoiled by O'Brian and Forester, and because my momentum from their series means I'll probably try the next book just to see if it's better. Maybe once Midshipman Bolitho grows up the quality of the writing will too.

text:

I am giving a 2 stars review because the speaker worked well while it lasted, which wasn't for very long. After approximately 3 months of gentle use, my Tough Fugoo started performing erratically.

Initially, the build quality appeared (?) to be very good, I liked that the speaker was relatively heavy with a good solid feel. Battery life performed as advertised, and sound quality, which is the reason I purchased the speaker, was better than any of the competition I had sampled, and the volume was more than adequate for a speaker of this size.

The problem I experienced is the Bluetooth mode turning off and on for no reason. Initially this would occur once or twice, and then it would play without any problems for the rest of the time it was used. Approximately one week after the problem started, it worsened, and became very frustrating. I tried resetting the speaker, and I also reloaded or re-installed the firmware, but no change.

I really thought I purchased the best mini-Bluetooth speaker out there. And never came even close to putting the Tough speaker to the test, as I had always treated it gently. It died and crapped-out all on it's own design and build quality.

When I contacted Fugoo via email, they returned a response within a few hours. I explained the problem, and was informed that I needed to replace the speaker unit. They requested proof that I purchased from an authorized dealer, and proof of date of purchase to show proof speaker was within the warranty period (12 months). Not the best way to treat a customer, especially considering the product line itself is less than the warranty period.

After I provided the requested information, I was informed that it would take 2 to 3 weeks and that I would be sent an RMA number. This was just over a 1 week ago, and I'm still waiting for the RMA number. No mention on how long I'd have to wait for an RMA, hopefully not an additional 2 to 3 weeks.

I anticipate getting a refurbished unit that crapped out on someone else. I won't be too happy about that, as mine was practically brand new, and pampered. Someday after I get the replacement, I'll do a follow up.

I am giving this four stars instead of five because a product shouldn't fail within thirty days, regardless of how good the support is. title: This is an important book
text: First of all, I should say that I spent the last 12 years of my career working at a hospital as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, so when I received this book as a present from a friend I was excited to read it. However, after reading it, I was mystified by some of the critical reviews I found on Amazon. As an RT I spent a lot of time with patients who had breathing problems. This included patients with COPD/emphysema and asthma who struggled to breathe. The standard treatment for these conditions is a class of drugs called bronchodilators. Inhaling these drugs can save people who are unable to breathe, but especially the more chronic patients often don't respond as their bodies seem to become immune to the effects of the drugs over time. With these patients, I would often teach them some of the breathing techniques described in this book. Often I had great success in calming these patients (they're panicked because their damaged lungs make it difficult for them to breathe) and getting them to slow down their respiratory rate. I also worked in cardiopulmonary rehab with both patients who were recovering from heart attacks and pulmonary patients. When we exercised I noticed that most of them had forgotten about their diaphragms and were unable to isolated this critical pulmonary muscle during exercise. Mr. Nestor discusses this in the book. By the way, subsequent research based on the Framingham study does correlate decreased Vital Capacity (total lung volume) with increased cardiovascular risk. In any case, this book does not purport to be a medical textbook and many of the stories are anecdotal and not supported by volumes of medical double-blind studies, but I don't believe that it was the author's intent to propose breathing techniques as a way to cure diseases like scoliosis or ADHD, or as some sort of panacea for curing all illness. In fact, in the Epilogue he says this. But the book is a fascinating journey through 10+ years of the author's research into a much ignored topic. I believe that we can all benefit from practicing the techniques in this book. In short, I like his advice on the "perfect breath": Breathe in through your nose for about 5.5 seconds, then exhale for 5.5 seconds. Practice this for a few minutes. To your health!

I wanted to love this device because the specs looked great on paper, but the build quality is an absolute joke. The biggest issue by far is the power button. It is incredibly flimsy and feels like it was made from the cheapest plastic available. From the very first day, it didn't have a satisfying click; instead, it felt mushy and unstable.

Within two weeks of normal use, the button started sticking. I would press it to turn the unit on, and it would stay depressed, forcing me to poke at it with a paperclip just to get it to pop back out. Now, it has completely collapsed inward and barely registers a press at all. I have to press it with extreme force and hit it at a specific angle just to get the device to boot up. For an electronics product at this price point, having a primary point of interaction fail this quickly is unacceptable.

It is frustrating because the actual performance of the device is decent, but what good is a piece of tech if you cannot even turn it on reliably? I should not have to baby a power button or worry that it will snap off the motherboard if I press it too hard. This is a massive failure in quality control and structural design. Save your money and buy something from a brand that actually invests in durable components. I will be returning this immediately and looking for a replacement that isn't held together by hope and cheap plastic.

Even for an adult, there is something deeply soothing and inspiring about the artistic style. It is clear that the illustrator put a tremendous amount of passion into this project. If you are looking for a book that will spark a child's imagination or if you simply appreciate high-quality artistic work, this is a must-have for your collection. I would reccomend this book to lovers of fantasy and minor romance.

title: Great but not for me
text:
The writing in James Baldwin's 1953 Go Tell It on the Mountain is as good as writing gets, but this book wasn't for me. It's told through the filter of the Christian religion and while that may hold much sociological interest to many, none of it was new to me, though it is fascinating to think about it: A Middle Eastern religion, transformed in Europe, exported from there to America and then forced on unwilling slaves from Africa. But growing up in a fairly diverse East Coast city and having been raised going to church until I was no longer required to, the religious aspects of this book didn't interest me. The only part of it I found compelling was Part Three in which that element was least present, which the section that described the main character's origin story.
 If you're interested and don't know a lot about the influence of the church on American Blacks, this book—its working title was "Crying Holy"—is for you. Otherwise, you might be more interested in Baldwin's other works.

 On a bright, summer day, bright in her memory forever, she came into the store alone, wearing her best white summer dress and with her hair, newly straightened and curled at the ends, tied with a scarlet ribbon. She was going to a great church picnic with her aunt, and had come in to buy some lemons. She passed the owner of the store, who was a very fat man, sitting out on the sidewalk, fanning himself; he asked her, as she passed, if it was hot enough for her, and she said something and walked into the dark, heavy-smelling store, where flies buzzed and where Richard sat on the counter reading a book.
 She felt immediately guilty about having disturbed him, and muttered apologetically that she only wanted to buy some lemons. She expected him to get them for her in his sullen fashion and go back to his book, but he smiled and said:
 "Is that all you want? You better think now. You sure you ain't forgot nothing?"

title: User-Friendly Design, But Tricky Connection
text:
The BEST feature here is the dedicated buttons for each function, as opposed to the “rocker” style most of these remotes have. Also, these buttons are silent (unlike some of the others which sound like clickers!)

Unfortunately, this unit has one thing to BEWARE of. While the Manual directions are very clear about how to pair the Movo with your phone or other device, you get NO INSTRUCTIONS WHATSOEVER regarding connection/regular usage! This is unfortunate since making a Bluetooth connection is QUITE TRICKY.

HERE IS HOW TO CONNECT THIS REMOTE TO USE IT (this assumes you have already paired it up with your phone as per the directions): 1. Don’t even bother to open Settings; 2. Simply hold down the red Power button—BUT KEEP HOLDING IT DOWN until it turns first RED, then it FLASHES GREEN, then it becomes SOLID GREEN, then finally turns RED again. 3. RELEASE the Power button just as the light turns RED again!

This is the ONLY WAY I have found that works every time, and it is fairly easy. FAIRLY easy! Practice it a couple of times if you are having trouble with the connection.

Also, be sure to TURN THE POWER OFF when you’re finished using the Movo by holding the Power button down awhile—until the light turns red and then goes out! This will save battery life.

Once you get the hang of using the Power button, I think you will find this remote is a good one.

For those reviewers who are disappointed in the writing, this is not meant to be great literature, it's just a very fun mystery, with colorful characters. It has me turning the pages, wanting to know what happens next.

A note to Amazon: a month between episodes is way too long. This is what I would call "light reading", and each episode takes maybe an hour to read. So I have to wait at least 5 months to finish reading what is a very short book? An episode a week would be much better. By the time each new episode arrives, I've long stopped thinking about the book. The point of a serial is to anticipate the next episode, not to forget about it.

What really sets this book apart, though, is how the illustrations manage to be both whimsical and sophisticated. As an adult, I found myself lingering on each spread, noticing details I missed the first time. The color palette changes with the mood of the story, making it an immersive experience for both child and parent. It’s the kind of book that will hold up through years of bedtime storytelling and still feel fresh.

If you are looking for a gift for a young child, or simply want to add a visually stunning title to your home library, I cannot recommend this enough. Beautiful illustrations truly make a book memorable, and this one delivers on every level. Five stars without hesitation.

However, I am giving it four stars instead of five because the power cord is a bit short. In my living room setup, I had to use an extension cord, which I generally try to avoid for safety reasons. But coming home doesn't solve the problem - only when the truth is revealed will her life and the lives of her friends and family finally be safe again.

Lynette Eason has done a wonderful job of building up a story that keeps readers turning pages, eager to solve the mystery of "who done what" as they cheer on Jillian. [Spoiler Alert]: One of my favorite aspects of this story is Colton's reaction to meeting his and Jillian's daughter. Even through his anger at missing the first ten years of his little girl's life, the love and acceptance he displays is truly moving.

title: Do buy
text:
I’ve been using Do Buy for about three weeks now, and I’m genuinely impressed with the results—enough to leave a solid 4-star review. First off, the texture is lovely: lightweight, absorbs quickly, and doesn’t leave any greasy residue. I have combination skin that’s prone to breakouts, and this hasn’t clogged my pores at all. In fact, I’ve noticed fewer small bumps and a more even tone since I started using it. The scent is subtle and fresh, not overpowering—thankfully, because strong fragrances often irritate my skin.

What I appreciate most is the hydration. My skin feels plump and softer in the morning, and makeup applies smoothly on top. I’ve also used it as a night treatment, and it seems to calm redness overnight. For the price point, it’s a great value compared to other products in this category.

Why only 4 stars? A couple of minor quibbles. The packaging is functional but not very elegant—the pump dispenser works fine, but the bottle feels a bit cheap for the price. Also, I wish it came with a little more product; I’m already halfway through and three weeks isn’t long enough to confirm long-term benefits. It’s too early to say if it will visibly fade my dark spots or fine lines, but so far, so good.

Overall, I’d recommend Do Buy if you want a gentle, effective hydrator that plays well with other products. Just don’t expect miracles overnight. I’ll likely repurchase, but I’ll keep an eye on how long the bottle lasts.

title: Noise Reduction Techniques
text:
There is a specific topic in this book that I have not seem covered in any of the 25+ book that I have on electromagnetic phenomena. The topic is the shield cut-off frequency of a coaxial cable. Common-mode currents at low frequencies (below a few hundred hertz) cause noise problems with coaxial cables, but signals above tens of kilohertz do not. This is vital data which is apparently not explained in many text books. For me, this topic justifies the cost of the text. Having said that, I am annoyed because the book is quite expensive relative to other books of its size and age. The point is that you have to buy it, but it is expensive to do so.
Even an advanced designer will benefit from this book, although you, like me, won't necessarily want to read all of it. It is sufficient to pick and choose areas of particular interest. The less advanced designer would clearly benefit more and the book would therefore represent better value for them. Given a choice between this one and Morrison's Grounding and Shielding Techniques in Instrumentation, pick this one. This one is more technically accurate and useful.

text: I’ve read my fair share of self-help books over the years, and most of them either feel like common sense dressed up in fancy jargon or they make you feel worse for not good enough for not being able to “just think positive.” This one is different. “The Power of Now, Is Taking Control of Your Emotions!” landed on my Kindle during a particularly rough patch at work and at home, and I honestly I was skeptical. Another book telling me to calm down? But the moment I started reading, something clicked. It doesn’t just tell you to control your emotions; it actually shows you how to step back from them and observe them without being consumed. The exercises are practical and surprisingly easy to fit into a busy day. I’ve always been someone who reacts first and thinks later, and that pattern has caused me a lot of regret. After working through the first few chapters, I found myself pausing before snapping at my kids or spiraling over a work email. That pause is everything. The author writes with a clear, grounded voice—no spiritual fluff or vague promises. It’s direct and actionable. My anxiety hasn’t vanished overnight, but I now have a real tool to keep it from running the show. I’ve recommended this to three friends already, and two have texted me saying it’s changing how they handle stress. If you’re tired of feeling like your emotions are driving your life, give this a real chance. It’s not a magic fix, but it’s the closest thing I’ve found to a practical manual for emotional freedom. Five stars without hesitation.

For the price, the sheer variety is impressive, and I’ve already used several pieces to prototype a couple of simple circuits. The breadboard is decent quality, and the jumper wires are flexible enough.

However, I’m knocking off one star for a few reasons. Some of the smaller resistors aren’t labeled clearly, so I had to double-check with a multimeter. If you already know your way around a breadboard and just need a big starter stash, this is a solid value. For total newbies, you’ll want to pair it with a tutorial book. title: Lacking in depth
text:
I really wanted to like this book. The premise was intriguing, and the early chapters had me hooked. But by the halfway point, I realized the author was just skimming the surface of what could have been a rich, complex story. The characters are sketched out with only the broadest of strokes—their motivations feel pasted on, their internal conflicts resolved with a single conversation. The world-building is similarly thin: we’re told about politics, history, and magic systems, but they never feel lived in or consequential.

What frustrates me most is the lack of depth in the central themes. The book gestures at weighty ideas—identity, power, sacrifice—but never digs into them. Every time it sets up a moral dilemma or a philosophical question, it either dodges it with a convenient plot twist or explains it away in a paragraph. I kept waiting for the narrative to slow down and wrestle with its own implications, but it just barrels forward on plot mechanics. The conflict feels manufactured; the stakes are high in theory but hollow in practice because we never truly understand why anyone believes what they do.

I’ve read other works by this author, and they handled nuance much better. This one reads like a rushed first draft that needed another round of revision to deepen the characters and the world. It’s not a terrible read—the prose is competent and the pacing keeps you turning pages—but I finished it feeling unsatisfied, as if I’d eaten a meal with no flavor. If you’re looking for something thought-provoking or emotionally resonant, look elsewhere. This is a shallow pool dressed up to look like an ocean.

text:
I purchased these colored contact lenses for a themed party, and for that specific purpose, they worked out great. The color is vibrant and really pops, which is exactly what I wanted to complete my costume. They have a slightly thicker feel than my prescription lenses, which makes them feel a bit more restrictive on the eye. If you are looking for something to wear for a full work week or long hours every day, I would suggest investing in a higher-end medical brand.

That being said, for a one-time event or a few hours of cosplay, they are a perfect choice. They are affordable and achieve the visual effect perfectly without breaking the bank. I didn't experience any major blurring of vision, just some mild discomfort toward the end of the evening. As long as you manage your expectations and use plenty of rewetting drops, you should be fine. I would definitely buy them again for another costume, but I will stick to my regular contacts for my everyday life.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
Colombian Latin alternative rockeros return to form with this outstanding album. The music is so good you don't even need to understand Spanish to get it. "Complemento," "Paces" and "Al Parque"are sure to appear in a future greatest hits compilation. These musical witch doctors have been concocting just the right amount of rock, Colombian folkloric music, Andean spiritual rhythms and Afro-South American beats for the perfect potion and they've never shared it with anyone (nor has any group been able to reverse engineer it). On "Oye" it's evident they still have the recipe carefully tucked away and the potion still has magical healing powers.

Though their creative trajectory has transformed them from punks to popstars to trip-hopsters (as captured on their appropriately titled and excellent greatest hits CD, "Evolucion/Evolution"), it's the first time they appear to be basking in nostalgia and taking a step back, which isn't necessarily a bad thing if you're the Aterciopelados. And it's especially not a bad thing when the album is reminiscent of their amazing 1997 release, "Pipa de la Paz." Though on this album, you won't catch former uber feminist and vocalist Andrea Echeverri who recently became a mom singing lyrics like: "I won't ruin my silhouette with a baby" as she did on "La Culpable" off the "Pipa" album.

The Latin alternative world can also exhale. Despite the lanky Echeverri and the mousy Hector Buitrago helping each other out on both of their recent solid solo efforts, the rumors ran rampant about an imminent break-up. Though Echeverri's Latin Grammy-nominated album of her same name had a commercial edge over Buitrago's "Connector," Buitrago demonstrated that he can take some calculated artistic risks and still pull off a successful avant-garde album.

To enjoy this album you don't need Spanish. You don't even need an open mind. All you need is good taste. Enjoy! --Mario I. Oña

title: Great for documents.  Horrible for photos. Get it on sale and it's a steal!
text:
If I could do it, it would be 3.5 stars. Here is the skinny:

Pros:

Scanning and printing of normal documents is great.

You can scan to a network folder, your computer, to FTP, to a USB stick, or email as an attachment right from the printer. It's more than reasonable for first page out and multiple pages.

Easy setup. Printing from your phone is easy. Internet printing capability (print from anywhere, ready when you get home).

Toner is like all color laser printers, relatively expensive for the brand name but much cheaper than inkjet in the end.

Have been successful faxing using a OBI200 and a Google Voice number so very handy when you need to occasionally fax but don't have a physical land-line in the house.

While it isn't silent, it is not unreasonably loud. My old Canon inject makes more racket (clicks, clacks, bangs) when it starts up.

I have never had wake from stand-by issues. Wakes from sleep pretty fast.

Cons:

It is big (small con). But all color lasers tend to be in this size and up as they need to be able to hold and align all those cartridges. As a matter of fact, due to the pull-out tray design and smaller physical cartridges this is probably on the smaller side of color laser printers.

Flatbed color scanning from your computer of things like photographs, is IMHO HORRIBLE, with out of whack colors and edge diffractions and all sorts of oddities. It's to the point that I wonder if it's defective. Oddly, scanning of documents seems pretty good. I need to do some experimentation to see if it's a software driver issue or something but I've scanned direct into Photoshop, Picassa, and Acrobat and they all are pretty sub-par. The computer driver scanning controls are now very basic, not like they used to be years ago with much more control...maybe that's part of the problem.

Also, when _printing_ photographic type images the colors are massively over-saturated...okay for presentation graphs, charts, and stuff but again waaaayy off base for anything else. While I understand this is a business oriented machine, even businesses scan/print photographs and it shouldn't be this far off (a lack of functionality/settings in the printer driver could be partly to blame).

The outer frame has a clean finish, and the built-in scoreboard with dry-erase surface is handy. For the price, the cabinet and board alone are a decent value.

The problem is the darts. This set comes with three sets of brass darts, and honestly, they are the weak link here. The shafts are plastic and break very easily. On my second night using them, one of the shafts snapped off at the barrel just from a normal throw hitting the board. The flights are cheap, too they lose shape after a few throws and don't even hold their position. The tips tight. The tips themselves seem okay but one came dull. I tried to play a serious game and within half an hour I had to swap out the darts for a set I already owned.

It feels like the manufacturer spent the budget on the cabinet and board, then just threw in the cheapest darts they could find. For a beginner who just wants to hang something on a wall, the cabinet and board are fine, but if you intend to actually play, plan on replacing the darts immediately. I gave it three stars because the board cabinet deliver on their promise. But if you are buying this mainly for the darts, you will be disappointed.
